ze.quest.0.title: Crash Landing
ze.quest.0.subtitle: Choose Your Supplies
ze.quest.0.des:
While exploring space, you crashed into this world, the 'Overworld', for reasons unknown. Luckily, your body is fine, but your spaceship was so badly damaged that you can't find it.

Fortunately, you managed to grab one supply crate during the crash. The problem is that you had no time to check what's inside, so you don't know what it contains, and it may even have been damaged by the impact so badly that you can't salvage anything.
ze.quest.0.reward: So, how is the supply crate you grabbed?
ze.quest.1.title: Loot Goblin
ze.quest.1.subtitle: Flint and Sticks
ze.quest.1.des:
First, let's make some tools to survive. Let's get some wood, the most useful thing to process.

Chopping trees by hand would take forever, so you need to make basic tools.

You can get sticks by breaking off the thicker branches of a tree, not the main trunk, and
flint can be obtained by digging gravel, with a chance of dropping. You can also dig dirt (without grass) and get flint with a certain chance.
ze.quest.2.title: RPG
ze.quest.2.subtitle: Power Up
ze.quest.2.des:
Press Alt+`(~) to open the stats screen of the Better Leveling mod. You can start by choosing one of three specializations: Combat, Mining, or Crafting, and each specialization has its own stats you can raise. You raise them with experience.

Unlocking another specialization costs 30 levels.

The Crafting specialization's Gardening skill may glitch out when applied to some crops. If you suspect that, try lowering the skill level to 0.
ze.quest.3_1.title: Swish Swish Swish Swish
ze.quest.3_1.subtitle: Flint Knife
ze.quest.3_1.des:
You can craft a flint knife by combining flint and a stick.

Knives are used for cooking, but they can also cut grass to get straw. You can also use one as a weapon in a pinch.
zs.quest.4.title: Weaving Nature Together
ze.quest.4.subtitle: Straw
ze.quest.4.des: When you cut grass and such with a knife, you have a chance to get straw. With it you can craft string, or a flint axe usable in the very early game.
ze.quest.5.title: Earthbreaker
ze.quest.5.subtitle: Flint Axe
ze.quest.5.des:
Now you can craft an axe that can chop trees.

Craft a flint axe by weaving together flint, a stick, and the straw you got with the knife.
ze.quest.6.title: The Giving Tree
ze.quest.6.subtitle: Logs
ze.quest.6.des:
At last, you can chop down trees. Cut the base of the tree and it will fall, giving you logs and other stuff.

Be careful not to get crushed by the falling tree.

To be fair, you could also just chop it with no axe at all. But that takes forever, doesn't it?
ze.quest.8.title: I! Can control the trees!
ze.quest.8.subtitle: Wooden Planks
ze.quest.8.des: You can process a log into 4 planks. Later, machines will let you get more planks from a single log.
ze.quest.9.title: The Artificial Sun Sailing Through Space
ze.quest.9.subtitle: Ship Power Plant [Fusion]
ze.quest.9.des:
(Translated by PDA) Nothing suits as a power generation facility inside a spaceship better than a fusion reactor. You seem to already have experience building one, so I won't give a long explanation.

Don't worry. The construction system will build the fusion reactor for you, too. As long as you have the materials, that is.
ze.quest.10.title: Workbench, Crafting Table, Who Cares
ze.quest.10.subtitle: Crafting Table
ze.quest.10.des: Combine 4 wooden planks to craft a crafting table. Place it down and right-click it, and you'll get a 3*3 crafting grid, bigger than the old 2*2 space, letting you craft a wider variety of things.
ze.quest.11.title: Now This Is Minecraft
ze.quest.11.subtitle: Wooden Pickaxe, Stone Pickaxe, and Furnace
ze.quest.11.des:
At the crafting table, craft a wooden pickaxe using wooden planks and sticks. Now you can mine stone and metal with a pickaxe.

Mine stone to get cobblestone, and use the cobblestone to craft a furnace so you can heat all sorts of things.

To mine harder things, you need to craft new pickaxes from stone and iron as the main materials.
ze.quest.12.title: Origin of Water
ze.quest.12.subtitle: Ship Fuel [Liquefied D-T Fuel]
ze.quest.12.des: (Translated by PDA) The fusion reactor's fuel is likewise D-T fuel. However, it needs to be liquefied to make it easy to store inside the ship.
ze.quest.13.title: Smog Generator
ze.quest.13.subtitle: Ship Backup Power Plant [Diesel Generator]
ze.quest.13.des:
(Translated by PDA) You need a backup generator to power up the fusion reactor, and in case the reactor shuts down in an unavoidable situation.

The diesel generator, which boasts a decent power output even if not on par with the fusion reactor, is a perfect fit.
ze.quest.14.title: Oil Baron
ze.quest.14.subtitle: Ship Backup Fuel [Diesel]
ze.quest.14.des: (Translated by PDA) This is the fuel for the ship's diesel generator, and it is also used for lighting fires.
ze.quest.15.title: The Best Defense Is a Good Offense.
ze.quest.15.subtitle: Ship Defense Weapon [Laser]
ze.quest.15.des:
(Translated by PDA) They're also there to power the ship's fusion reactor, but space has all sorts of hazards. Meteors usually hit the hull, or space pirates attack.

Let's hope your ship's lasers only slice up the meteors.
ze.quest.16.title: Metal Combo
ze.quest.16.subtitle: Ship Base Materials
ze.quest.16.des: (Translated by PDA) The ship's base materials use aluminum, nickel, steel, and HOP graphite.
ze.quest.17.title: Precious Partner
ze.quest.17.subtitle: Traveler's Backpack
ze.quest.17.des:
Your inventory is probably running out of space by now. ...Or it ran out a long time ago. Anyway, once you can process wood, you can craft a backpack.

Early on, you're given several options: a version with a fluid tank or without, and a version with a sleeping bag or without. The versions with a tank and sleeping bag need extra materials including iron, so I recommend the ones without for now.

Wear it in the back slot of the Curios inventory (top left of the inventory character), and after that you can open the backpack with Alt+E.

The main features: put a tool in the tool slot, the leftmost of the top buttons, and hold X to swap to it, and press the button between the backpack and inventory to use the sleeping bag right away.

If you can afford it, you'll be able to upgrade it at the smithing table later.

You can equip the sleeping bag by right-clicking a placed backpack while sneaking.
ze.quest.18.title: Monkey Business
ze.quest.18.subtitle: Grappling Hook
ze.quest.18.des:
There's a tool you need to explore this vast, harsh world: the grappling hook.

All you need is string and an iron pickaxe.

Hold it and left-click to fire the grappling hook and anchor it, then while sneaking you can climb up and down with W and S. And when the rope is at its shortest, you can jump to release the grapple. Detailed controls are written in the item description.
ze.quest.19.title: Enhanced Coal
ze.quest.19.subtitle: Coke Oven
ze.quest.19.des:
To process coal or charcoal more efficiently, you need a coke oven.

This machine needs a 3*3*3 space. Place coke bricks in a 3*3*3 shape, then right-click the center with the 'Engineer's Hammer' you'll get as a reward to finish it.

Processing with coke produces creosote oil as a byproduct, and when it's full, the oven stops working. You need this creosote oil to make treated wood, so I recommend stockpiling it.
ze.quest.20.title: Blast Furnace (Immersive Engineering)
ze.quest.20.subtitle: Blast Furnace
ze.quest.20.des:
At this point, to smelt steel yourself you need a blast furnace. Build it the same way as the coke oven.

Put coke in as fuel and put in iron, and smelting begins.

The slag that comes out as a byproduct... is used as a building material or as fertilizer for the Garden Cloche.

Are you stuck because the materials require Nether materials? You can make obsidian yourself with a bucket trick, open a Nether portal, and gather resources. It's by no means impossible.

There's an even simpler way. Go down as far as you can. To a depth of around -61. If you stay there long enough, the power of the dimension will swallow you. To come back, just do the opposite.
ze.quest.21.title: Steel Engineer
ze.quest.21.subtitle: Steel Ingot
ze.quest.21.des:
Steel, which outperforms iron, is needed in large quantities as a material for gear and machines. At this point you can obtain it through the blast furnace (Immersive Engineering).

A pickaxe made from this material can break obsidian. It's the perfect material if you'd hate to waste diamonds.

If you've reached the point of smelting this metal, you've come far enough that you no longer have to worry about making a living.


Having adapted to the Overworld somewhat, while exploring the crash site you luckily find some communication devices among the ship's parts that might still be usable. Set up a beacon to announce your location to other alien factions, and connect communications with the radio kit.
ze.quest.22.title: Create
ze.quest.22.subtitle: Andesite Alloy and Casing
ze.quest.22.des:
You're ready to handle Create machines. Some structures in this world already hold this technology, so you can salvage it, but to use it properly you need to know how to craft it too.

Most Create machines run on rotational force and have an intuitive look (and the lag that comes with it). And on most items (machines), you can hover the cursor and hold W to bring up a dedicated guide window.

First, craft the core materials of Create machines: andesite alloy and casings. You can craft the alloy by combining steel pieces and andesite. Don't make too much. Later you'll be able to make it with more efficient methods.

An andesite casing can be crafted by right-clicking andesite alloy on a placed stripped log. Or you can craft 4 andesite casings from 4 treated planks and one andesite alloy to save alloy.
ze.quest.23_1.title: Manpower
ze.quest.23_1.subtitle: Hand Crank
ze.quest.23_1.des:
The simplest way to make rotational force is to turn it yourself. Attach it to a shaft or a machine's shaft and keep holding right-click to supply rotational force.

But the speed and torque are weak, so later you'll need other methods. And it's tedious, too.
ze.quest.23.2.title: Power Transmission
ze.quest.23.2.subtitle: Shafts and Cogwheels
ze.quest.23.2.des:
These are the basic elements used to transmit rotational force. To be precise, they transmit torque (force) and speed.

If the speed is slow and frustrating, use this method early on.
Mesh a small cogwheel with a large cogwheel, then connect that small cogwheel's shaft to another large cogwheel's shaft. Then mesh another small cogwheel, and you'll see the last small cogwheel spinning faster than the very first large cogwheel.

The catch is that torque and speed are usually inversely proportional: for example, even from the same source with the same power, if you take it at a higher speed the torque decreases, and conversely if you take stronger torque the speed decreases.
ze.quest.23.3.title: Water Breathing, Second Form
ze.quest.23.3.subtitle: Water Wheel
ze.quest.23.3.des:
The water wheel, one of the basic power generators, literally generates power using flowing water.

Just touching flowing water (any liquid, to be precise) gives it constant speed and torque.

If you additionally craft it once more with 8 planks, you can make a large water wheel that is slower but provides more torque.
ze.quest.24.title: Pressing Matters
ze.quest.24.subtitle: Mechanical Press
ze.quest.24.des:
When it receives rotational force, it compresses the item placed beneath it.

Just dropping the item on the floor works, but for a cleaner setup, place the item on a depot, then place the press above it and run it.

If you use a basin instead of a depot, you can compress multiple items into one. A typical example is compressing 9 iron ingots into an iron block.
ze.quest.25.title: Modular Workbench
ze.quest.25.subtitle: Mechanical Crafter
ze.quest.25.des:
It can do the crafting a regular crafting table can, and by enlarging it you can also make things that can only be crafted in the mechanical crafter.

To get brass, you have to mix copper and zinc at a 1:1 ratio, and there are several ways. You can combine two molten metals in a Tinkers' smeltery, craft it with Create's mixer and blaze burner, or get it from Immersive Engineering's alloy kiln.
ze.quest.26.title: Workplace Accident Generator
ze.quest.26.subtitle: Crushing Wheel
ze.quest.26.des:
It can grind up as many items as its size allows. To work, the two wheels must rotate in opposite directions, and items must be fed in from the correct direction.

It can also be placed sideways and still works. Of course, you'll need other devices like belts too.

For reference, you can put in ore to get crushed raw ore and byproducts. And if you then run that crushed raw ore through a fan, you can get different byproducts from those you'd get in a Tinkers' melter.
ze.quest.27.title: Summer Essential
ze.quest.27.subtitle: Encased Fan
ze.quest.27.des:
Just place it and give it rotational force, and it will push or pull entities. But what you can do depends on what's in front of the fan.

If there's water, it washes items; if there's lava, it smelts items. If there's fire, it smokes (cooks) items, and if there's soul fire, it transforms items.
ze.quest.28.title: The Magic Wand of Cogwheel Land
ze.quest.28.subtitle: Wrench
ze.quest.28.des:
This simple yet important tool is needed when handling most Create machines.

It rotates machines, and you can also right-click while sneaking to pick a machine up instantly, among other things. It's a tool that's a huge pain to go without.
ze.quest.29.title: Auto Clicker
ze.quest.29.subtitle: Deployer
ze.quest.29.des: It can perform left-clicks or right-clicks, and you can hand it an item to make it do the job you want.
ze.quest.30.title: Fluid Dynamics
ze.quest.30.subtitle: Fluid Tanks, Fluid Pipes, and More
ze.quest.30.des:
These are the means of storing or transporting liquids. Power a mechanical pump and you can transport liquids through pipes.

Note that a pump only moves liquid over a certain distance, so if you need to transport it farther, you must install another pump partway along.
ze.quest.31.title: Industrial Revolution
ze.quest.31.subtitle: Belt
ze.quest.31.des:
Stretch it over shafts and give the shafts rotational force, and the belt runs in that direction, carrying entities such as items on top.

It can't be connected at any angle other than right angles and 45 degrees.
ze.quest.32.title: Stone Breaker
ze.quest.32.subtitle: Mechanical Drill
ze.quest.32.des: Give it rotational force and it breaks stone and the like in front of it.
ze.quest.33.title: Interacting With Moving Structures
ze.quest.33.subtitle: Portable Storage Interface and Redstone Contact
ze.quest.33.des:
The Portable Storage Interface is mainly used to insert or extract items on a moving structure. While it is giving or receiving items, the structure stops until the item transfer is complete.

The Redstone Contact outputs a redstone signal whenever they meet each other.
ze.quest.34.title: Essentials for Automated Farming
ze.quest.34.subtitle: Mechanical Saw and Mechanical Harvester
ze.quest.34.des:
The saw not only cuts the trees in front of it, but also processes wooden items when they're thrown at it. Also, processing logs gives you more planks than crafting them by hand. However, since it can make other outputs, I recommend setting a filter.

The harvester harvests fully grown plants in front of it, and replants them if the connected inventory has the matching seeds.

To use these in an automatic farm, you need to attach them to a moving structure.
ze.quest.35.title: Essentials for Moving Structures
ze.quest.35.subtitle: Super Glue and Bearings
ze.quest.35.des: To build a moving structure, one of Create's signature features, connect the blocks you want with super glue and give rotational force to things that can move structures, such as a bearing.
ze.quest.36.title: Steve the Diver
ze.quest.36.subtitle: Diving Set
ze.quest.36.des:
If you want to explore underwater, you'll want to wear this gear.

A copper diving helmet worn together with a copper backtank consumes air underwater and grants water breathing.

Place the copper backtank down and power its shaft, and it slowly recharges with air.

These two pieces are enough, but if you want to move underwater as if you were on land, you need copper diving boots. Copper diving boots make you sink to the bottom quickly instead of floating, and let you jump underwater.
ze.quest.37.title: Fluid Dynamics (Side Story)
ze.quest.37.subtitle: Hose Pulley and Portable Fluid Interface
ze.quest.37.des:
The Hose Pulley is useful for efficiently moving (placed) liquid from deep places. Basic pipes can also transport it through pumps, but if you need to pump up lava or the like from deep down, rather than extending pipes all the way down there, you can just use this hose pulley.

The Portable Fluid Interface is used to insert or extract liquids on a moving structure. While it is giving or receiving liquid, the structure stops until the liquid transfer is complete.
ze.quest.38.title: Steampunk 2025
ze.quest.38.subtitle: Steam Engine
ze.quest.38.des: A device that outputs powerful rotational force (torque). It can be mounted on a fluid tank made of 4 or more connected tanks, and it runs when you keep supplying water to the tank and there's a heat source such as a campfire or a blaze burner beneath the tank.
ze.quest.39.title: Mix and Match
ze.quest.39.subtitle: Mechanical Mixer
ze.quest.39.des:
Place it above a basin and give it rotational force above a certain speed to run it.

In its normal state it can only mix items, but with the blaze burner you'll craft later, you'll be able to make a wider variety of things.
ze.quest.40.title: Calcifer
ze.quest.40.subtitle: Blaze Burner
ze.quest.40.des:
Hold an empty blaze burner and right-click a blaze or a blaze spawner to complete the blaze burner.

In its basic state it performs on par with a campfire or worse, but if you feed it item-form fuel it generates high heat. And if you feed it special fuel, it enters a superheated state.
ze.quest.41.title: Pseudo-Semiconductor
ze.quest.41.subtitle: Precision Mechanism
ze.quest.41.des: Precision mechanisms, crafted using the deployer, are used as key components in Create's advanced machines and in the Immersive Engineering machines you'll tackle later.
ze.quest.42.title: Shaping Up
ze.quest.42.subtitle: Rolling Mill
ze.quest.42.des: Used to turn metal and the like into rods or wires.
ze.quest.43.title: Boing
ze.quest.43.subtitle: Extendo Grip
ze.quest.43.des:
While held, it extends your interaction range. It still works if you hold it in your off hand and use the item you want in your main hand.

Using it wears down its durability, though. If you're wearing a Backtank, the air in the Backtank is used up first instead of the durability.
ze.quest.44.title: Pouring Lava on Obsidian
ze.quest.44.subtitle: Sturdy Sheet
ze.quest.44.des:
Pour lava onto Powdered Obsidian and press it twice with a Mechanical Press to make a Sturdy Sheet.

This sheet is a key material for building trains, and it's also a component for Immersive Engineering machines.
ze.quest.45.title: Choo-Choo
ze.quest.45.subtitle: Train Assembly Kit
ze.quest.45.des:
Lay down the tracks and connect a Train Station to them, and the track work is done.

Then enable assembly mode at the Train Station and the track turns blue. Place a Train Casing on top and a small Bogey gets installed. Now decorate the train with whatever blocks you like, including the Train Controls, glue it together with Super Glue, then press the assemble button at the Train Station and the train is ready to run.

If you just want to ride the rails temporarily, you can place a Handcar straight onto the track and use it.
ze.quest.46.title: Hiring a Conductor
ze.quest.46.subtitle: Train Schedule
ze.quest.46.des:
Write up a train operating plan with a Train Schedule, then hand it to a Blaze Burner placed on the train or an animal sitting in a train seat, and that entity gets appointed as the conductor.

The appointed conductor runs the train according to the schedule.
ze.quest.47.title: Kinetic Conversion
ze.quest.47.subtitle: Alternator
ze.quest.47.des:
Converts rotational force into electricity.

Power output depends on speed (and yes, it's proportional, obviously).

Electricity is needed to run machines from other mods, including Immersive Engineering, which we'll cover later.
ze.quest.48.title: Lorentz Force
ze.quest.48.subtitle: Electric Motor
ze.quest.48.des: You can also go the other way and turn electricity back into rotational force.
ze.quest.49.title: Electrical Engineering
ze.quest.49.subtitle: Battery, Connectors, and Wires
ze.quest.49.des:
Batteries can store electricity, and just like Fluid Tanks, you can expand their capacity as a multiblock.

To transport electricity you need connectors and wires. Place a connector at the sending point and another at the receiving point, then link them with a Wire Coil. After that, use a Wrench to configure input/output on the connectors.

The wire determines how much power can be transferred, and connectors vary by type too.
ze.quest.50.title: Wealth Redistribution
ze.quest.50.subtitle: Tunnel
ze.quest.50.des:
When you need to sort items traveling on a belt into different directions, you need a Tunnel.

An Andesite Tunnel only sends out one item at a time in the other directions.

A Brass Tunnel can send out lots of items at once, and you can apply filters so only the set items go through each direction.
ze.quest.51.title: Logistics
ze.quest.51.subtitle: Item Vault, Funnels, and Chutes
ze.quest.51.des:
An Item Vault has less storage per space than a chest, but it can be expanded into one big single storage. However, a lone Item Vault can't have items put in or taken out by itself. That's where Funnels come in.

An Andesite Funnel can put in and take out small amounts of items from a connected machine or storage.

Unlike the Andesite Funnel, a Brass Funnel can move far more items at once, and you can apply filters so only the set items pass through.

A Chute works like a hopper, dropping items from above downward. It can connect diagonally, and with an Encased Fan you can even send items the opposite way, from bottom to top.

The Smart Chute adds a filter function and a quantity function.
ze.quest.52.title: The Giant
ze.quest.52.subtitle: Windmill Bearing and Windmill Sails
ze.quest.52.des: You can attach blocks like Windmill Sails in front of a Windmill Bearing. The more blocks used as sails, the more rotational force (stress) it produces.
ze.quest.53.title: Not Enough Ammo
ze.quest.53.subtitle: .45-70 Ammo
ze.quest.53.des: Ammo is useless without a gun, and a gun is useless without ammo.
ze.quest.54.title: The Trapdoor Gun
ze.quest.54.subtitle: Springfield 1873 Trapdoor Rifle
ze.quest.54.des:
A classic firearm that's just as simple to craft.
It can only be loaded one round at a time, but it packs quite a punch early on.

Press R to reload, right-click to aim, and left-click to fire.
Press V for a melee attack and Ctrl to go prone.
ze.quest.55.title: Sniper Born in Heaven
ze.quest.55.subtitle: Vintage Springfield Scope
ze.quest.55.des:
The only scope that can be mounted on the Springfield 1873 Trapdoor Rifle.

Hold the gun and press Z to open the gun modification screen and attach it.

Crouching while aiming holds your breath and reduces screen sway, but hold it too long and the sway gets worse for a moment.
ze.quest.56.title: I Am the Kiln
ze.quest.56.subtitle: Alloy Kiln
ze.quest.56.des:
Stack Kiln Bricks in a 2x2x2 shape, then right-click with an Engineer's Hammer to finish it.

The Alloy Kiln can smelt basic metals into alloys.
ze.quest.57.title: Burning Golden Blood
ze.quest.57.subtitle: Blaze Blood
ze.quest.57.des:
A premium fuel used in the fuel tanks of Smelteries and Melters.

It burns hotter than lava, so you can smelt high-tier metals and alloys.

To make it, put a Blaze into a Smeltery or Melter. If that's too much trouble, you can melt a Blaze Skull or Ichor Crystal, a crystal found in the Nether.
ze.quest.58.title: Doping
ze.quest.58.subtitle: Blaze Cake
ze.quest.58.des: Used as Blaze Burner fuel. A Blaze Burner that eats this cake gives off much more heat, which is used in recipes that need superheated conditions.
ze.quest.59.title: Immersive Engineering
ze.quest.59.subtitle: Redstone Engineering Block
ze.quest.59.des:
You're ready to handle Immersive Engineering machines. Using Create machines, you've surely reached the point where you can gather basic resources and craft advanced materials.

Unlike Create, Immersive Engineering machines use electricity. Early on, you'll need to hook up power generated by an Alternator. Explanations of this mod's machines and tools are in the 'Engineer's Manual' you'll receive as a reward.

Most Immersive Engineering machines are multiblocks (for example, the Coke Oven and the Blast Furnace). They may offer less freedom than Create machines, but they're more efficient to match. They do eat a lot of steel, so smelting plenty of steel in advance is recommended.

Each machine has ports, and their roles are shown by color. Red ports take redstone signals to turn the machine on and off, blue-ish ones take in items, fluids, etc., and orange-ish ones output items, fluids, etc. Yellow is where the power goes in.

The Redstone Engineering Block is used as a component in most Immersive Engineering machines. To craft it, you have to use Create machines. Looks like Create's retirement just got postponed.
ze.quest.60.title: Fluid Dynamics v2
ze.quest.60.subtitle: Fluid Pipe, Fluid Pump, and Fluid Router
ze.quest.60.des:
The special thing about Immersive Engineering's Fluid Pipes is that a single pipe can carry multiple kinds of fluid. That's handy when you need to pull several fluids out of one output port.

Connect a Fluid Pump in the middle of a pipe and give it power and a redstone signal to speed up fluid transport. It can also absorb adjacent fluids.

The Fluid Router sends fluid that enters it out in the direction of the filter color you set. You can pull in a fluid shown in EMI to set it.

By the way, with Immersive Engineering's fluid machines, you can right-click some input/output ports directly with a bucket to add or remove fluids.
ze.quest.61.title: Finger-Mangling Accident Generator v2
ze.quest.61.subtitle: Crusher
ze.quest.61.des:
Crushes items and such, and when you crush ore you also get that ore's byproduct. For example, put in Raw Iron and you get Iron Dust plus a chance at one more Iron Dust.

Check the Engineer's Manual for the recipe, or search for the Crusher.
ze.quest.62.title: Juicing
ze.quest.62.subtitle: Squeezer
ze.quest.62.des:
Mostly used to squeeze plants for their juice.

Check the Engineer's Manual for the recipe, or search for the Squeezer.
ze.quest.63.title: Noise That Shakes Heaven and Earth
ze.quest.63.subtitle: Arc Furnace
ze.quest.63.des:
This huge furnace produces intense heat to smelt various metals. Besides alloys, ores also get a higher chance of extra byproducts than smelting them in the Crusher.

Check the Engineer's Manual for the recipe, or search for the Arc Furnace.

To run it you need power plus 3 Graphite Electrodes attached. You can get the 'Arc Furnace Electrode' blueprint from a villager and craft finished electrodes at the Engineer's Workbench, or make slightly damaged ones with the Metal Press. A HOP Graphite Ingot can be made by compressing 2 HOP Graphite Dust at extremely high heat. After that, a single HOP Graphite Dust is enough to process one in the Arc Furnace.

Anyway, once it starts running... it's ridiculously loud. Using an Extreme Sound Muffler is recommended. You can mute any sound you want by clicking the speaker icon in your inventory or pressing the hotkey (Numpad /).
ze.quest.64.title: Factory Grunt's Desk
ze.quest.64.subtitle: Engineer's Workbench
ze.quest.64.des:
A workbench for crafting things you can't make in a regular crafting table, or making them more efficiently.

What you can craft depends on the type of blueprint placed on it. For example, with the 'Component' blueprint on it, you can craft machine parts you'll be making a lot of later using fewer resources.
ze.quest.65.title: Industrial Revolution v2
ze.quest.65.subtitle: Conveyor Belt
ze.quest.65.des: A belt you can place as a block, and it likewise transports items or entities. The Extraction Conveyor Belt can pull items out of an attached chest or machine.
ze.quest.66.title: About to Rot
ze.quest.66.subtitle: Fermenter
ze.quest.66.des:
Ferments certain plants to make ethanol.

Check the Engineer's Manual for the recipe, or search for the Fermenter.
ze.quest.67.title: Refining
ze.quest.67.subtitle: Refinery
ze.quest.67.des:
Mixes one or more fluids, or uses an item as a catalyst, to refine them into another fluid.

Check the Engineer's Manual for the recipe, or search for the Refinery.
ze.quest.68.title: Fill 'Er Up
ze.quest.68.subtitle: Bottling Machine
ze.quest.68.des:
Fills buckets or anything that can hold fluid.

Check the Engineer's Manual for the recipe, or search for the Bottling Machine.
ze.quest.69.title: Composite Thermosetting Plastic
ze.quest.69.subtitle: Duroplast
ze.quest.69.des:
In the Refinery, put in ethanol and a Silver Plate to process acetaldehyde, then refine that with Creosote Oil to make Phenolic Resin. Then pour it into the Bottling Machine with a Metal Press Mold: Plate to craft it.

Duroplast is used later when crafting Composite Circuits.
ze.quest.70.title: Circuit
ze.quest.70.subtitle: Composite Circuit
ze.quest.70.des:
Can be crafted at the Engineer's Workbench using the Component blueprint.

It's a material needed to craft Mekanism machines.
ze.quest.71.title: Highly Ordered Pyrolytic Graphite
ze.quest.71.subtitle: HOP Graphite Ingot
ze.quest.71.des:
A material you can only get by compressing a large amount of Coke Dust and processing it at high heat.

Crafting it normally takes 4 HOP Graphite Dust, but with the Arc Furnace, just one is enough.

It's a material needed to craft Mekanism machines.
ze.quest.72.title: Mind Your Fingers
ze.quest.72.subtitle: Metal Press
ze.quest.72.des:
Shapes metals and the like to match the Metal Press Mold.

Molds can be crafted at the Engineer's Workbench using the Mold blueprints.

Check the Engineer's Manual for the recipe, or search for the Metal Press.
ze.quest.73.title: Blast Furnace v2
ze.quest.73.subtitle: Advanced Blast Furnace
ze.quest.73.des:
It's cooler than the old Blast Furnace. It also adds dedicated input/output ports and lets you attach add-ons that make the furnace run faster.

Check the Engineer's Manual for the recipe, or search for the Advanced Blast Furnace.
ze.quest.74.title: Blast Furnace DLC
ze.quest.74.subtitle: Blast Furnace Preheater
ze.quest.74.des: Can be attached to both sides of the Advanced Blast Furnace, and supplying it with power speeds up the furnace.
ze.quest.75.title: In Search of Black Gold
ze.quest.75.subtitle: Seismic Survey Tool
ze.quest.75.des:
To find oil, you need a Seismic Survey Tool. Place it on the ground, load a Shotgun Shell, and activate it, and the shell fires into the ground and records the shockwave.

Use the seismic results to check for reservoirs, including oil, nearby. Dots will gradually spread out widely from the black dot in the center, and if there's a reservoir, there will be an unnaturally empty patch with almost no dots. That's the sign of a reservoir.

Not every reservoir is oil, though. You need to check the seismic results for that chunk to see which fluid is there. If you found oil, check the next quest.
ze.quest.76.title: A Blender Without Blades
ze.quest.76.subtitle: Mixer
ze.quest.76.des: Mainly mixes items into a fluid to process it into a new fluid.
ze.quest.77.title: Sticking in a Straw
ze.quest.77.subtitle: Derrick
ze.quest.77.des:
Once you've found a chunk with oil, you need to build a machine to extract it.

Place the Derrick and connect power, and it shows the items it needs. Prepare Fluid Pipes, water, and liquid concrete.

Once the Derrick has connected its pipe to the oil deposit, be ready to store the oil gushing out under pressure. Otherwise the oil spills and is lost.

If the oil has all gushed out or never came out at all, read the Pumpjack quest below.
ze.quest.78.title: Sucking the Marrow Dry
ze.quest.78.subtitle: Pumpjack
ze.quest.78.des: If you remove a Derrick that no longer produces oil, there will be a concrete-wrapped pipe on the ground. Place a Pumpjack on it properly and run it, and the Pumpjack pumps out the remaining oil.
ze.quest.79.title: Gald Cup
ze.quest.79.subtitle: Distillation Tower
ze.quest.79.des:
Distills crude oil into 4 kinds of oil. Since these four oils come out of a single output port, using a Fluid Pipe (Immersive Engineering), which can carry multiple fluids in one pipe, or a Fluid Router is recommended. Bitumen also comes out as residue, and when it fills up, the Distillation Tower stops working.

Lubricant can be sprayed on some machines to boost their speed. It can also be refined into Sulfurated Diesel in the Hydrotreater.
Sulfurated Diesel can be used as fuel as-is, but you can also extract the sulfur separately with the Hydrotreater to refine it into Diesel.
Kerosene can be distilled once more into Sulfurated Diesel and Benzene.
Naphtha can be refined with Benzene into Gasoline in the Refinery, or into LPG in the Hydrotreater.
ze.quest.80.title: Sulfur, Get Out
ze.quest.80.subtitle: Hydrotreater
ze.quest.80.des:
Typically it consumes water to extract sulfur from Sulfurated Diesel, and it's also used to refine other oils.

Water goes in from the top, and oil goes in from the side.
ze.quest.81.title: Not a Rice Cooker
ze.quest.81.subtitle: Coker
ze.quest.81.des:
Mixes Bitumen with water to process it into Sulfurated Diesel and Petcoke. You can get the Petcoke from the two spots at the bottom of the machine, and the Sulfurated Diesel can be taken from the front output (orange). This Sulfurated Diesel has a different composition from the Sulfurated Diesel from the Distillation Tower, so they don't mix. Further processing into regular Diesel is recommended.

Petcoke can be used the same way as regular Coke.

Also, if you craft Steel Casing using a Petcoke Block, you get twice as many as the normal recipe.
And compressing Petcoke Dust at extreme heat gives Fluorite Dust.

The Coker is a seriously huge multiblock machine. There are a lot of confusing parts while building, so it's recommended to give up your shaders for a bit and build it using a projector.
ze.quest.82.title: Mekanism
ze.quest.82.subtitle: Steel Casing
ze.quest.82.des:
You're ready to handle Mekanism, the technology from the world you came from. You'll have to pour in all the machines and resources you've made so far.

Mekanism machines are high-tech, so most of them deliver great performance in relatively little space. Also, power is transported through pipes rather than wires, which makes it relatively stable.

Using a Petcoke Block, you can make two Steel Casings.
ze.quest.82.des2: Some Mekanism machines (structures) are multiblocks. If you're curious about the detailed build, hover over the structure's main material and hold W. You'll get a guide similar to Create's. Besides that, you can preview how to stack it layer by layer in the multiblock's main block's uses (EMI).
ze.quest.83.title: Gas Can
ze.quest.83.subtitle: Jerrycan
ze.quest.83.des:
A portable fluid container with a capacity of 1,000 mB (10 buckets). To fill it with fluid, though, you have to use a machine (e.g., the Fluid Injector).
Combine it with a tool that needs fuel and it fuels the tool right away.
ze.quest.84.title: Eco-Friendly
ze.quest.84.subtitle: Biodiesel
ze.quest.84.des: A high-efficiency fuel processed from plants.
ze.quest.85.title: Environmental Pollution
ze.quest.85.subtitle: Diesel Generator
ze.quest.85.des:
Burns oil to produce loud noise and power.

Since the output power is large, you need to use wire-based transmission equipment or something like Mekanism's Energy Cube.
ze.quest.86.title: My Drill Is the Drill That Will Pierce the Heavens... Er, the Floor!
ze.quest.86.subtitle: Mining Drill
ze.quest.86.des:
A portable drill that runs on oil. It's mainly used for mining, and the tier of blocks it can mine and its mining area depend on the drillhead.

You can attach a drillhead at the Engineer's Workbench, and various upgrades too.
ze.quest.87.title: I'm Not Going to Raven Holm...
ze.quest.87.subtitle: Buzzsaw
ze.quest.87.des:
A portable saw that runs on oil. It's mainly used to chop down trees, and depending on the saw blade it can cut stone too.

You can attach a saw blade at the Engineer's Workbench, and various upgrades too.
ze.quest.88.title: Thanks, Dinosaurs!
ze.quest.88.subtitle: (Sulfurated) Diesel
ze.quest.88.des:
A fuel you get by distilling oil, and with further processing you can remove the sulfur. If you can't be bothered, you can just use it as-is. You only lose a little.

By the way, they say most oil actually came from some kind of trees rather than dinosaurs, but dinosaurs are more interesting than trees, so... let's drop this debate.
ze.quest.89.title: Let's Become One.
ze.quest.89.subtitle: Applied Energistics
ze.quest.89.des:
(Translated by PDA) To commemorate our first meeting, our engineering team has decided to share storage technology with you: Applied Energistics (AE).

We actually learned of this technology by chance from a meteorite that fell from beyond this world. Unfortunately, no such meteorite has been detected in the Overworld. So we'll help you get started with AE technology.

By the way, please handle the budding Certus Quartz carefully. Most AE technology relies on the Certus Quartz that grows from these blocks as a key material. If you break them carelessly, their purity will decrease.

Once things improve, you'll be able to buy more of the things needed for AE technology from us.

If you're interested in AE, we'll provide you with information about it on your PDA.
ze.quest.90.title: Cramming Education
ze.quest.90.subtitle: Metallurgic Infuser
ze.quest.90.des:
A machine mainly used to infuse metals with substances to make alloys and such.

You can also infuse an Iron Ingot with Carbon twice to craft Steel. Later, if you process Carbon efficiently with a machine called the Enrichment Chamber, you can make Steel using fewer resources than the old method.
ze.quest.91.title: Just As I Modified It
ze.quest.91.subtitle: Configurator
ze.quest.91.des: Mainly used to adjust the input/output of Mekanism machines or pipes, or to remove them safely. Hold it in your hand and hold B to select the mode you want.
ze.quest.92.title: Fluid Dynamics v3
ze.quest.92.subtitle: Mechanical Pipe and Fluid Tank
ze.quest.92.des: A pipe-type way to transport fluids, with good transport speed even without a separate pump.
ze.quest.93.title: Industrial Revolution v3
ze.quest.93.subtitle: Logistical Transporter and Bin
ze.quest.93.des: A pipe-type way to transport items. The Bin is a storage that can hold a huge amount of a single item.
ze.quest.94.title: Electrical Engineering v2
ze.quest.94.subtitle: Universal Cable and Energy Cube
ze.quest.94.des: A pipe-type way to transport power.
ze.quest.95.title: Electrolysis
ze.quest.95.subtitle: Electrolytic Separator
ze.quest.95.des: A machine that splits fluids or gases using electricity.
ze.quest.96.title: Gas Dynamics
ze.quest.96.subtitle: Pressurized Tube and Chemical Tank
ze.quest.96.des: A pipe-type way to transport gases.
ze.quest.97.title: Boiling Water
ze.quest.97.subtitle: Thermal Evaporation Plant
ze.quest.97.des:
A device that evaporates water with solar heat to get brine. This large device has to be built as a multiblock. Build instructions are on the next page.

The Thermal Evaporation Valve can take in or output fluids, and it can also receive heat.

Open up the ceiling so the device can see the sky, supply water, and once the temperature exceeds 300K, the supplied water turns into brine. Temperature varies with the time and the biome where the device is built. If you want to supply more heat, you can place an Advanced Solar Generator on a corner of the top layer or feed heat into the Thermal Evaporation Valve.

If you don't have the resources for an Advanced Solar Generator yet, a Resistive Heater can produce heat directly from electricity.
ze.quest.97.des2:
As in the picture below, lay a 4x4 floor with Thermal Evaporation Block, then build walls on top with Thermal Evaporation Block, including the Thermal Evaporation Controller and Thermal Evaporation Valve. Make sure to fill the corners too. Then place 8 Thermal Evaporation Blocks on the top layer (that is, excluding the corners) and it's done.

Once finished, a screen shows up on the Thermal Evaporation Controller and redstone particles appear across the whole device.

The items required by the quest are the amounts needed for the minimum-size device, and you can build it taller (up to 18 blocks) if you want. You can also replace the non-corner parts with Structural Glass to see inside.
ze.quest.98.title: Space Heater
ze.quest.98.subtitle: Resistive Heater
ze.quest.98.des: A machine that converts electricity into heat. Heat can be output through the green ports on both sides.
ze.quest.99.title: Thermodynamics
ze.quest.99.subtitle: Thermodynamic Conductor
ze.quest.99.des: A pipe-type way to transport heat.
ze.quest.100.title: Gas Gas Gas!
ze.quest.100.subtitle: Chemical Reaction Chamber
ze.quest.100N.des: A machine that mixes two gases to create a new gas.
ze.quest.101.title: Vaporize/Liquefy
ze.quest.101.subtitle: Rotary Condensentrator
ze.quest.101.des: A machine that converts liquids into gases and vice versa.
ze.quest.102.title: Oxidation
ze.quest.102.subtitle: Chemical Oxidizer
ze.quest.102.des: A machine that oxidizes solid materials into gas.
ze.quest.103.title: Double Trouble
ze.quest.103.subtitle: Enrichment Chamber
ze.quest.103.des:
A machine that doubles ore (blocks) into dust. It does more than just ore processing, too.

For example, you can process redstone to be fed into a Metallurgic Infuser, or materials used for carbon, through the Enrichment Chamber at a much higher efficiency. Normal redstone only fills 10mB, but Enriched Redstone, made by enriching a single redstone in the Enrichment Chamber, fills 80mB. That's nearly 8x the efficiency, folks.
ze.quest.104.title: Triple Threat
ze.quest.104.subtitle: Purification Chamber and Crusher
ze.quest.104.des:
The Purification Chamber is a machine that triples ore (blocks) into clumps using oxygen.

You can get oxygen by putting water into an Electrolytic Separator.
The Crusher turns things into dirty dust and does other things too.

Afterwards, you can refine it into regular dust with the Enrichment Chamber.
ze.quest.105.title: Quad Damage
ze.quest.105.subtitle: Chemical Injection Chamber
ze.quest.105.des:
The Chemical Injection Chamber is a machine that quadruples ore (blocks) into shards using hydrogen chloride.

You can get hydrogen chloride by putting salt into a Purification Chamber, or by combining hydrogen and chlorine in a Chemical Reaction Chamber. You can get chlorine by putting brine into an Electrolytic Separator.

Afterwards, process it into clumps with the Purification Chamber, into dirty dust with the Crusher, and then refine it into dust with the Enrichment Chamber.
ze.quest.106.title: High Five (x5)
ze.quest.106.subtitle: Chemical Dissolution, Washing, and Crystallizing Chambers
ze.quest.106.des:
The Chemical Dissolution Chamber is a machine that processes ore (blocks) into dirty slurry, 1,000mB at a time, using sulfuric acid gas.
The Chemical Washer is a machine that uses water to wash dirty slurry into clean slurry.
The Chemical Crystallizer is a machine that processes 200mB of clean slurry into a crystal.

You can make sulfuric acid gas by feeding sulfur straight into the Chemical Dissolution Chamber. Alternatively, process it into sulfur dioxide in the Chemical Oxidizer, combine it with oxygen in the Chemical Reaction Chamber to make sulfur trioxide, then combine that in the Chemical Reaction Chamber with water vapor made by vaporizing water in the Rotary Condensentrator.

A good way to get sulfur is to extract it from sulfurized diesel, produced by processing oil, using a Pressurized Refinery Column.

Afterwards, process it into shards with the Chemical Injection Chamber, into clumps with the Purification Chamber, into dirty dust with the Crusher, and finally refine it into dust with the Enrichment Chamber.
ze.quest.107.title: Dynamic Tank-ing
ze.quest.107.subtitle: Dynamic Tank
ze.quest.107.des:
A multiblock tank that can store massive amounts of liquid or gas.

Input and output are possible through structural blocks.

It can be built as shown in the picture below, and every face except the edges can be replaced with a Dynamic Valve or Structural Glass. To increase capacity, just make it bigger. As long as it's a hollow cuboid, it can be built from a minimum of 3*3*3 up to a maximum of 18*18*18.
ze.quest.109.title: Tank
ze.quest.109.subtitle: Fluid Tank
ze.quest.109.des:
A multiblock structure that can hold more liquid than a Create Fluid Tank of the same size. You can pump liquid in from the top or bottom, and give a redstone signal to the bottom port to drain it.

Check the Engineer's Manual or search for Fluid Tank to see how to craft it.
ze.quest.110.title: Bulk Storage, One Item Type
ze.quest.110.subtitle: Item Silo
ze.quest.110.des:
A multiblock structure that can store a lot of one type of item. You can insert items from the top (needs extras like a hopper), and give a redstone signal to the bottom to extract items.

Check the Engineer's Manual or search for Item Silo to see how to craft it.
ze.quest.111.title: Not Exactly a Swimming Pool
ze.quest.111.subtitle: Oil Tank
ze.quest.111.des:
A tank that can hold more oil than a regular tank, and it's expandable too.

Check the Engineer's Manual or search for Oil Tank to see how to craft it.
ze.quest.112.title: Not Quite Draconic, But...
ze.quest.112.subtitle: Induction Matrix
ze.quest.112.des:
A multiblock battery that can store far more power than an Energy Cube.

Inside the matrix you need Induction Cells to store power and Induction Providers to send and receive power. For input/output, you also need to set the Induction Ports' I/O mode with a Configurator.

It can be built as shown in the picture below, and every face except the edges can be replaced with Induction Ports or Structural Glass. To increase capacity or I/O rate, upgrade the tier or number of cells. As long as it's a cuboid, it can be built from a minimum of 3*3*3 (but since the Induction Cell and Provider go inside, one axis is 4) up to a maximum of 18*18*18.
ze.quest.113.title: I'll Burn the Sea of Stars!
ze.quest.113.subtitle: Geothermal Generator
ze.quest.113.des: Generates power from burnable items or liquids, or generates a small but infinite amount from the heat of adjacent lava. You can pull power out through the green port on the side.
ze.quest.114.title: Heartbreaker
ze.quest.114.subtitle: Wind Generator
ze.quest.114.des: Produces power in proportion to the Y level it's placed at.
ze.quest.115.title: The Giving Sun
ze.quest.115.subtitle: Solar Generator
ze.quest.115.des: Produces power if it has an open sky and receives sunlight.
ze.quest.116.title: The Sun Gives Even More
ze.quest.116.subtitle: Advanced Solar Generator
ze.quest.116.des: An upgraded Solar Generator that can also be used as a heat source for the Thermal Evaporation Plant.
ze.quest.117.title: Go Touch Some Grass... and Work Out!
ze.quest.117.subtitle: Dynamo
ze.quest.117.des:
The Dynamo is one of the early-game ways to produce electricity the Immersive Engineering way.

Connect a windmill or a water wheel to the side (the big black circle), and when they spin, they convert that motion into electricity. Attaching Windmill Sails to the windmill blades increases efficiency further.
A windmill is most efficient in open air, and spins faster in windy rain or thunderstorm weather, producing more power.

A water wheel's efficiency changes depending on the water flow it touches.
ze.quest.118.title: Hot Iced Americano
ze.quest.118.subtitle: Thermoelectric Generator
ze.quest.118.des: Generates electricity the bigger the temperature difference between the blocks or liquids placed on its sides. For which blocks affect temperature, search for Thermoelectric Generator in the Engineer's Manual.
ze.quest.119.title: Walk Tall Anywhere
ze.quest.119.subtitle: Free Runners
ze.quest.119.des:
When charged and worn, they cancel fall damage by using electricity (this doesn't apply to damage from falling into the void). They can also automatically step up one-block ledges.

Press ,(<) to change modes or toggle them on and off.
ze.quest.120.title: Walk Tall Anywhere v2
ze.quest.120.subtitle: Armored Free Runners
ze.quest.120.des: Adds armor to the Free Runners for extra defense.
ze.quest.121.title: Human Rocket
ze.quest.121.subtitle: Jetpack
ze.quest.121.des:
When filled with hydrogen and worn, you can press the Space Bar to burn hydrogen and fly.

Press K to change modes or toggle it on and off. In normal mode you only rise while holding the Space Bar; in hover mode, you keep burning hydrogen to hold the height you rose to, and you can descend by sneaking.
ze.quest.122.title: Human Rocket v2
ze.quest.122.subtitle: Armored Jetpack
ze.quest.122.des: Adds armor to the Jetpack for extra defense.
ze.quest.123.title: Atomic Science
ze.quest.123.subtitle: Hazmat Suit Set
ze.quest.123.des:
Welcome to nuclear fission-level technology. Now you can process uranium into fuel, generate heat from it, and spin turbines to produce enormous amounts of power. And even more importantly, you can refine the nuclear waste left after fission to get polonium, plutonium pellets, or antimatter.

You'll need room for two big multiblock structures and assorted small production machines. If the reactor gets damaged or something goes wrong, the radiation that leaks out will contaminate the surrounding chunks, so I recommend building it somewhere well away from your main base. Well, if you're confident, feel free to ignore that.

On top of the materials for the multiblock structures, you'll need to prepare a large amount of water, plus uranium and fluorite.

Before you start, put on the Hazmat Suit Set to protect yourself against any radiation leaks.
ze.quest.124.title: The Actual Power Plant
ze.quest.124.subtitle: Industrial Turbine
ze.quest.124.des:
Spins turbines with steam pressure to produce lots of power. It takes in steam (gas) through two or more Turbine Valves and outputs the spent steam as water (liquid).

If the power is full and can't be output, it stops working.
ze.quest.124.des2:
First, I recommend placing it close to the reactor.

Make the outline with Turbine Casing, then place a Turbine Rotor in the center and attach Turbine Blades. Put a Rotational Complex directly above the Turbine Rotor and surround it with Pressure Dispersers.
Then stack Electromagnetic Coils and Saturating Condensers on top of that, and wrap the outside with Vents. To finish, place Turbine Valves and Structural Glass or Turbine Casing on the remaining faces.

Once it's all done, redstone particles will appear. Note that this is just an example size; you can make it bigger or smaller.
ze.quest.125.title: Meltdown
ze.quest.125.subtitle: Fission Reactor
ze.quest.125.des:
Burns nuclear fuel to produce enormous heat. This boils coolant (water) into steam. Through the Reactor Ports you must feed in nuclear fuel (gas) and coolant (liquid), and output the steam (gas) from the vaporized coolant and the nuclear waste (gas) produced from burning the fuel.

If the coolant drops to 0 or below while running, the reactor will take damage and begin leaking radiation.
ze.quest.125.des2:
First, I recommend placing it close to the Industrial Turbine.

Make the outline with Reactor Casing, lay the floor with Reactor Glass or Reactor Casing, then stack Fuel Assemblies on top of it so that they don't face each other.

Place a Control Rod Assembly on top of the Fuel Assemblies, and wrap the remaining faces with Reactor Ports and Reactor Glass or Reactor Casing.

Once it's all done, redstone particles will appear. Note that this is just an example size; you can make it bigger or smaller.

By the way, nuclear waste can't be transported with the Quantum Entangloporter. So it's best to build the reactor in the Overworld.
ze.quest.126.title: Crafting Nuclear Fuel
ze.quest.126.subtitle: Isotopic Centrifuge
ze.quest.126.des:
To make nuclear fuel in the Isotopic Centrifuge, you need uranium hexafluoride.

It's made by combining hydrofluoric acid and uranium oxide in a Chemical Reaction Chamber.

You can get hydrofluoric acid by dissolving fluorite in sulfuric acid gas in a Chemical Dissolution Chamber, and you can get uranium oxide by enriching Uranium Ingots in an Enrichment Chamber to get uranium dust and oxidizing that in a Chemical Oxidizer.

Fluorite can be found as an ore underground, and if you process oil, you can also make it by compressing 9 Petroleum Coke Dust at ultra-high temperature.
ze.quest.127.title: Waste Management
ze.quest.127.subtitle: Solar Neutron Activator, Pressurized Reaction Chamber, and Radioactive Waste Barrel
ze.quest.127.des:
Nuclear waste can be processed into polonium in the Solar Neutron Activator, or into plutonium in the Isotopic Centrifuge.

Process polonium and plutonium in a Pressurized Reaction Chamber along with water and fluorite dust to get polonium and plutonium pellets. Spent nuclear waste is produced in these processes.

If you store spent nuclear waste in a Radioactive Waste Barrel, 1 unit of waste is removed per second.

All the gases produced in this process are radioactive, so please handle them with care.

Nuclear waste can't be transported with the Quantum Entangloporter. So it's best to place both the reactor and the waste processing facility in the Overworld.
ze.quest.128.title: Fission Checklist
ze.quest.128.subtitle: Running the Reactor
ze.quest.128.des:
Now you need to connect Pressurized Tubes or Mechanical Pipes to each machine and device. Make sure the tubes or pipes you use are Ultimate tier to be safe. Otherwise, the transfer rate can't keep up with the throughput, and that causes radiation leaks.

First, you need to connect the reactor and the Industrial Turbine. Sneak and right-click the port that will output coolant (steam) with a Configurator to switch it to coolant output mode, and connect it to a Turbine Valve with a Pressurized Tube. Next, connect the water (liquid) from the Industrial Turbine's vent to a reactor port set to input-only mode with a Mechanical Pipe. That completes the connection between the reactor and the turbine.

Then pre-fill another input-only port on the reactor with water so the coolant is loaded in advance. Next, connect the port in nuclear waste (gas) output mode to a waste processing device such as the Solar Neutron Activator.

Finally, you need to connect a Universal Cable to the Turbine Valve that will output the electricity produced by the Industrial Turbine; I recommend connecting it to an Induction Matrix in case the power fills up. And for the very, very last step, supply nuclear fuel (gas) through a reactor port that accepts it, and you're all set.
ze.quest.128.des2:
Right-click the reactor to open its interface, click the info icon on the left, set the max burn rate appropriately (15 recommended), then come back and press Activate to start the reactor. On the first run, the water in the coolant tank may get consumed, but under normal conditions it'll stop at a certain level. (If it keeps dropping, just SCRAM it and lower the burn rate.)

If everything works properly and there's no radiation leak, congratulations. Lots of power and advanced materials are now yours. And a little bit of anxiety, too.
ze.quest.129.des3:
Note that this is a water-cooled setup using only the reactor and the turbine. If you build a Thermoelectric Boiler between the reactor and the Industrial Turbine and connect it, you can use sodium cooling. At the same scale, it cools the reactor's heat more efficiently than water cooling.

Lastly, the Geiger Counter I gave you as a reward displays the current chunk's radiation level and the time until the radiation clears, while the Dosimeter displays the radiation dose of yourself or whatever you right-click.
ze.quest.129.title: Gun Imports
ze.quest.129.subtitle: Gun Durability
ze.quest.129.des:
The more you fire a gun, the more its durability wears down. (The same goes for attachments.)
The lower the durability, the worse the gun's overall stats get.

You can repair it on an Anvil using steel as the material.

For most guns, the lower the durability, the higher the chance of a malfunction, and if a malfunction (Jam) happens, you can press J to inspect the gun and clear the jam.
ze.quest.130.title: Crafting Antimatter
ze.quest.130.subtitle: Supercritical Phase Shifter
ze.quest.130.des:
It looks like you can now craft antimatter, something you couldn't even pull off in your own world.

Build a Supercritical Phase Shifter and feed it enough (a LOT of) power and polonium to produce antimatter. Spend 1000mB of it in a Chemical Crystallizer to get an Antimatter Pellet.

Production speed too slow? That's mostly because you don't have enough power.
ze.quest.130.des2:
It has to be built as a 7*7*7 sphere. Make the outline with SPS Casing and fill every face with SPS Ports and Structural Glass or SPS Casing.

You need at least 3 ports in total. There must be an input-mode port for polonium and power, and an output-mode port to send out the antimatter (gas). You can change these by sneaking and right-clicking the port with a Configurator.

The important part is that the port receiving power must have an Supercharged Coil attached on the opposite side, or it won't work.
ze.quest.131.title: AE Type Charger
ze.quest.131.subtitle: Charger
ze.quest.131.des: Charges items by pumping AE-unit power into them. If you don't have a proper power source, you can attach a Wooden Crank on top and turn it to produce a small amount of power.
ze.quest.132.title: Don't Overcharge It!
ze.quest.132.subtitle: Charged Certus Quartz Crystal
ze.quest.132.des: Charging a Certus Quartz Crystal in the Charger gives you a Charged Certus Quartz Crystal. This crystal carries its own electric charge and is used to craft certain items. For example, throw it into water along with a few ingredients and you can get a new resource.
ze.quest.133.title: Quartz Is Being Duplicated?!
ze.quest.133.subtitle: Budding Certus Quartz
ze.quest.133.des:
Certus Quartz is an essential resource for building AE devices, and it's generated by Budding Certus Quartz, much like amethyst.

Budding Certus Quartz comes in several grades with different budding speeds, and except for the Flawless grade, every other grade degrades with each bud until it eventually stops budding. If you mine Budding Certus Quartz with a pickaxe, you'll get quartz one grade lower. If you mine it with a pickaxe enchanted with Silk Touch, you'll get the original grade, but if it was top-grade quartz, it gets demoted to the one-step-lower Flawed grade.

Place it as carefully as possible; if needed, it seems wise to mine it with a Silk Touch pickaxe.

If you want a cheeky trick: hold a pickaxe in your main hand and a Mekanism Cardboard Box in your off hand and right-click the quartz to pack it. You can mine it to pick it up, and when you place it where you want and sneak-right-click, the contents are placed exactly as they were. Regardless of grade.

(Message translated by PDA) You can now purchase the highest-grade quartz from us!
ze.quest.134.title: Broker
ze.quest.134.subtitle: Energy Acceptor
ze.quest.134.des: Some AE machines and the ME system use a power system called AE units. You need this device to use power from other mods' machines.
ze.quest.135.title: Overcharge? What's That?-
ze.quest.135.subtitle: Fluix Crystal
ze.quest.135.des: If you throw a Charged Certus Quartz Crystal, redstone, and Nether Quartz into water (or some other liquids), the electricity discharges from the Certus Quartz and it turns into a Fluix Crystal. Fluix Crystals are used to build AE devices, mostly power-related ones.
ze.quest.136.title: Fiber Optic Cable (Not)
ze.quest.136.subtitle: Fluix ME Glass Cable
ze.quest.136.des: The basic cable of the AE power system. It carries not only power but also ME system data.
ze.quest.137.title: Not For Its Intended Use
ze.quest.137.subtitle: Vibration Chamber
ze.quest.137.des: If you haven't managed to build a proper generator yet, this will help. When you burn a burnable item in it, resonance occurs inside and generates AE power. It's decent as an emergency generator.
ze.quest.138.title: Crystal Kicker
ze.quest.138.subtitle: Growth Accelerator
ze.quest.138.des:
Attach it to Budding Certus Quartz and keep feeding it AE power to noticeably speed up the quartz production of the attached quartz. It works on amethyst too.

Note that it only receives power from the top and bottom.
ze.quest.139.title: Alien Semiconductor Tech
ze.quest.139.subtitle: Inscriber
ze.quest.139.des:
Break down the mysterious cube with a pickaxe to obtain five types of presses.

These circuit presses let you craft circuits and processors. They're used as basic components of AE machines.
ze.quest.140.title: FYI, There's No Channel System Here.
ze.quest.140.subtitle: ME Controller
ze.quest.140.des: The ME Controller, the heart of the ME system and the core of this tech, also acts as an Energy Acceptor, lets you see all connected devices at once, and shows the system's overall power status.
ze.quest.141.title: Charger
ze.quest.141.subtitle: Charging Station
ze.quest.141.des:
Charges tools and other items that need to be charged with power.
Connect power to the back or bottom and put in the item to charge, and charging begins.

Three tubes on the front glow, and their color shifts from red-ish to green in proportion to the charge level.
ze.quest.142.title: Osmium
ze.quest.142.subtitle: Osmium Compressor
ze.quest.143.title: Re-fined Obsidian
ze.quest.143.subtitle: Refined Obsidian Ingot
ze.quest.143.des:
A material used for parts and ingredients of advanced machines. Infuse obsidian dust with diamond and add osmium to complete it.

It can be processed with the Osmium Compressor.
ze.quest.144.title: Key Ingredient of Teleportation
ze.quest.144.subtitle: Teleportation Core
ze.quest.144.des:
Using the quantum entanglement singularity, you can now use teleportation technology.

Or... you could throw it into an overgrown well and open a door to a new world.
ze.quest.145.title: Tesseract
ze.quest.145.subtitle: Quantum Entangloporter
ze.quest.145.des:
A transport method that can send items, liquids, power, gases, heat, and more over long distances (regardless of distance or dimension).

Quantum Entangloporters on the same frequency connect to each other.

By the way, nuclear waste can't be transmitted.
ze.quest.146.title: Portal
ze.quest.146.subtitle: Teleporter
ze.quest.146.des:
A Teleporter is a device that instantly moves entities, including players, to a selected Teleporter.

Connect 7 or more Teleporter Frames to a Teleporter (big enough for a person to fit through) to give it a portal look, and set the destination Teleporter to open the portal. If you want to come back, connect Teleporter Frames the same way to the Teleporter at the destination.

The Portable Teleporter is a tool that lets you pick a Teleporter on the channel you want and go straight there. If you only want to teleport using the Portable Teleporter, you don't need Teleporter Frames.

The required power is proportional to the distance between Teleporters, and you can't travel farther than the power stored in the Teleporter allows.
ze.quest.147.title: The Real Miner, For Real
ze.quest.147.subtitle: Digital Miner
ze.quest.147.des:
Set the area and the blocks to mine, and it digs up blocks within the area.

You can supply power through the ports on both sides, and right-clicking to open the UI shows a bunch of buttons.

It can automatically send and receive items through ports connected to the back or top, and you can also set whether Silk Touch is applied to the mined blocks.

To use it properly, press the config button and set the area to mine and what to mine. The radius is the horizontal range centered on the miner, and the min and max set the height range.

You have to set which blocks the Digital Miner mines. Inverse mode lets it mine everything except the blocks you set, but that wastes power and time. Press Add New Filter to specify items. If you only want it to mine ores, choose a tag and enter forge:ores and it'll mine every ore.

Once you save the filter you're ready to go, but if you start it right away, it only mines ores, so the spots where ores were become empty gaps and unwanted mob spawns can occur. To fix this, set a replacement item (block) in the bottom-left slot and supply it to the Digital Miner, and the miner will place that block in the spot after mining.
ze.quest.148.title: It's Over 9000... Density!
ze.quest.148.subtitle: Matter Condenser and Singularity
ze.quest.148.des:
The Matter Condenser is a device that condenses items or liquids. Depending on the settings, you can just use it as a trash can, or make ammo for the Matter Cannon. But the most important thing is that it can make singularities.

To make a Matter Ball or a Singularity, you need storage components to hold the items and liquids to be condensed. For a singularity you have to put in 256,000 worth of matter, so you need at least a 64k ME Storage Component.

To put matter into the Matter Condenser, you can hand-feed items, or use belts or pipes to feed in items and liquids.
ze.quest.149.title: Quantum Mechanics
ze.quest.149.subtitle: Quantum Entangled Singularity
ze.quest.149.des:
Throw a singularity and an Ender Pearl or Ender Dust on the ground as items and set off an explosion, and you can craft a pair of Quantum Entangled Singularities.

Using these singularities, you can craft devices that teleport you across space, and with one pair of these singularities you can link an ME system wirelessly over long distances.

Think the quest icons overlap? Isn't that just quantum tunneling?
ze.quest.150.title: ME Quantum Network
ze.quest.150.subtitle: ME Quantum Ring and Link Chamber
ze.quest.150.des:
Place an ME Quantum Link Chamber and surround it with ME Quantum Rings to complete a Quantum Network Bridge.

Connect this to an ME system and attach one of a pair of Quantum Entangled Singularities, then build the same Quantum Network Bridge at the location you want and insert the remaining Quantum Entangled Singularity, and it links up with the ME system from afar, even transmitting AE power.

It even works across dimensions.
ze.quest.151.title: Fluid Disk
ze.quest.151.subtitle: ME Fluid Storage Cell
ze.quest.151.des:
Can store liquids, up to 18 types and 1024 bytes.

If the cell is empty, hold it in your hand and sneak-right-click to disassemble it into an ME Storage Component.

Increasing the capacity doesn't increase the number of storable types.
ze.quest.152.title: Item Disk
ze.quest.152.subtitle: ME Storage Cell
ze.quest.152.des:
Can store items, up to 63 types and 1024 bytes.

If the cell is empty, hold it in your hand and sneak-right-click to disassemble it into an ME Storage Component.

Increasing the capacity doesn't increase the number of storable types.
ze.quest.153.title: Gas Disk
ze.quest.153.subtitle: ME Chemical Storage Cell
ze.quest.153.des:
Can store gases, up to 5 types and 1024 bytes.

If the cell is empty, hold it in your hand and sneak-right-click to disassemble it into an ME Storage Component.

Increasing the capacity doesn't increase the number of storable types.
ze.quest.154.title: Disk Storage
ze.quest.154.subtitle: ME Drive
ze.quest.154.des:
One of the main technologies of the ME system is turning objects into data and storing them in cells.

To connect those cells directly to the ME system and manage them, you need to install them in an ME Drive.
ze.quest.155.title: Moving Data
ze.quest.155.subtitle: ME I/O Port
ze.quest.155.des:
You'll need this device to move contents between drives.

You can move the data of cells in an ME Drive to the ME I/O Port, or the other way around.

It'll mostly be used when moving contents to a bigger drive.
ze.quest.156.title: From Now On, Your Name Is ME Storage
ze.quest.156.subtitle: ME Storage Bus
ze.quest.156.des:
If you want to hook your old storage chest into your ME system, just slap on this ME Storage Bus and you're done.

No need to bother crafting storage cells. Of course, for sheer capacity you'll still end up making cells eventually.
ze.quest.157.title: Monitor
ze.quest.157.subtitle: ME Crafting Terminal
ze.quest.157.des: Well, technically it's a monitor plus a keyboard and mouse. You need this terminal to put things into or pull things out of the ME system. Make it a Crafting Terminal and you can craft right there too.
ze.quest.158.title: Contactless Warehouse
ze.quest.158.subtitle: ME Wireless Access Point and Wireless Crafting Terminal
ze.quest.158.des:
No need to walk all the way to a terminal just to move items. Place an ME Wireless Access Point, charge a Wireless Terminal and link it, and you can access the ME system remotely. However, access points have a maximum range, so you'll need to install Wireless Boosters to extend it.

The range grows in proportion to the number of boosters installed. The power usage goes up too, though.

Put it in a curios slot and press Ctrl+`(~) to open the wireless terminal instantly.
ze.quest.159.title: Unlimited Range
ze.quest.159.subtitle: Infinity Booster Card
ze.quest.159.des:
Stacking more and more wireless boosters costs a ton of power and resources, so just craft one pricey card and plug it in instead.

With the Infinity Booster Card installed, you can connect from anywhere in the same dimension, and it only demands a little extra power.
ze.quest.160.title: Unlimited Range+
ze.quest.160.subtitle: Quantum Bridge Card
ze.quest.160.des:
The only downside of the Infinity Booster Card is that you can't connect across dimensions. Fix that by spending even more resources on an upgrade.

The power requirement is the same as the Infinity Booster Card.
ze.quest.161.title: First Steps of ME Autocrafting
ze.quest.161.subtitle: ME Pattern Encoding Terminal and Blank Pattern
ze.quest.161.des:
You're ready to set up autocrafting, one of the main reasons people use AE in the first place.

First, put a Blank Pattern into the ME Pattern Encoding Terminal and encode the recipe of the item you want to register for autocrafting. You can place items you own or drag them in from EMI (the items shown on the right). Once it's complete, click the encode pattern icon to imprint the pattern.

You can register more than just crafting table recipes: machines including furnaces, smithing tables, and stonecutter recipes can be registered too.

To register furnace or machine recipes, click the furnace icon and then register the inputs and outputs. Unlike the other crafting patterns, you have to register these manually, which comes down to how this style of autocrafting works.
ze.quest.161.des2:
The crafting table icon (Crafting Patterns) mode loads the recipe as-is, so the recipe is applied exactly. However, you need a separate machine for this crafting.
The furnace icon (Processing Patterns) mode of autocrafting works on a 'no idea what this machine does, but put this in and this comes out' basis, so when autocrafting, it feeds in the inputs and waits for the items to come out of the machine and into the ME system. If the pattern isn't written correctly, the autocrafting job will wait forever.

The remaining icons imprint patterns the same way as the crafting table icon, but actually work no differently from the furnace icon.
ze.quest.162.title: Calculator
ze.quest.162.subtitle: Crafting Storage and Co-Processing Unit
ze.quest.162.des:
When you run autocrafting, the Crafting Storage handles calculating the materials needed, the quantity of results, and where to supply the materials. The more complex the ingredients, the more capacity the Crafting Storage needs.

The Co-Processing Unit isn't mandatory, but if you attach it to a Crafting Storage, it's an auxiliary processor that lets multiple crafts run at the same time whenever possible.

These only work when connected in the shape of a solid rectangular cuboid.
ze.quest.163.title: Logistics Sergeant
ze.quest.163.subtitle: ME Pattern Provider
ze.quest.163.des:
When an autocrafting request comes in with a pattern imprinted in the ME Pattern Provider, it supplies materials to the adjacent machine, making autocrafting possible.

You can attach it as a block to feed every machine on its touching faces, or as a panel to affect just one block.

Autocrafting starts once the ME Pattern Provider supplies materials to that machine, and the job counts as finished only when all the results have returned to the ME system by any means, including the Pattern Provider.

With the ME Pattern Access Terminal you'll get as a reward, you can manage every pattern connected to the ME system.
ze.quest.164.title: Auto Crafting Table
ze.quest.164.subtitle: Molecular Assembler
ze.quest.164.des: If you're going to autocraft crafting table recipes, this machine is pretty much essential. Supply it with AE power, and when the adjacent ME Pattern Provider sends it an autocrafting command and pattern, the Molecular Assembler grabs the materials on its own and outputs the result back to the ME system through the Pattern Provider.
ze.quest.165.title: Tricky Block Placing and Breaking
ze.quest.165.subtitle: ME Annihilation Plane and Formation Plane
ze.quest.165.des: Simply put, the Annihilation Plane breaks the block it faces or absorbs items and stores them in the ME system. The Formation Plane pulls a configured item from the ME system and places it or drops it as an item. They're a bit tricky to use, though.
ze.quest.165.des2:
The Annihilation Plane can be enchanted. Fortune and Silk Touch work the way you'd expect, while Efficiency and Unbreaking reduce the power the plane uses when it operates. 

You can't configure which blocks to break on the plane itself; instead, you have to set a filter on the connected storage. To use this properly, set it up through a separate, isolated chest: for example, attach an ME Storage Bus (an Import Bus won't work) to the chest and specify the block the Annihilation Plane should break. Then connect the Annihilation Plane to it, and it will only break the configured block.
If you want to keep those in the ME system, you can bring the items into the ME system with an Import Bus on another face. Also, when configuring the block, don't go by the placed block; go by the item the Annihilation Plane gets from breaking it. For example, breaking a stone block drops cobblestone, so you'd configure cobblestone. Naturally, if the Annihilation Plane has Silk Touch, you'd configure the stone block itself.
ze.quest.165.des3: It's easier to think of the Formation Plane as a storage rather than an output device. First, you can set the item to place or drop. Then, give it a higher priority than other storages through Priority (wrench icon), and supply that item to the ME system for it to work.
ze.quest.166.title: ME Intake
ze.quest.166.subtitle: ME Interface
ze.quest.166.des: A device for storing items output from external machines into the ME storage system. It can store items, fluids, and gases. Strictly speaking, think of it as a connector between the ME storage system and external pipes or belts. But since it's only a connector, it can't pull anything out of a chest or machine on its own.
ze.quest.167.title: ME I/O Device
ze.quest.167.subtitle: ME Import/Export Bus
ze.quest.167.des:
The ME Import Bus and Export Bus handle input and output for the ME system.
The ME Import Bus pulls items, fluids, gases, etc. from externally connected chests or machines and stores them in the ME system.

The ME Export Bus is the reverse: set what you want to extract on the bus, and the registered things from the ME system get stored in the connected chest or machine.
ze.quest.168.title: The Forest Where the Sun Never Sets
ze.quest.168.subtitle: Twilight Forest
ze.quest.168.des:
If you've gotten a Teleportation Core with the help of the alien forces or crafted one yourself, you can head to another dimension.

As in the example below, make a 2*2 floor of dirt, then surround it on top with a border of 8 dirt. Then plant flowers or grass on top and fill the pit with water, and you're all set. Now throw the Teleportation Core into that water, thunder and lightning will strike, and a portal to another world will open.
ze.quest.169.title: Proper Ammo Storage
ze.quest.169.subtitle: Ammo Box
ze.quest.169.des:
Storing ammo in an Ammo Box effectively saves inventory space. However, one Ammo Box can only hold one type of ammo. Put it in an appropriate slot in your inventory or curios tab, and ammo is supplied automatically when you reload your gun.

To put ammo in or take it out, right-click the ammo or an empty slot while holding the Ammo Box in your inventory.

Iron tier Ammo Boxes can hold 3 stacks, gold tier 6 stacks, and diamond tier up to 9 stacks.
ze.quest.170.title: Iron Rods and Springs
ze.quest.170.subtitle: Gun Workbench
ze.quest.170.des:
Most guns can be crafted at this Gun Workbench.

It mainly requires steel-based materials and springs. Depending on the performance (features), additional materials are required.
ze.quest.171.title: Lead and Gunpowder
ze.quest.171.subtitle: Ammo Workbench
ze.quest.171.des:
Most ammo can be crafted at the Ammo Workbench.

The required materials differ for each ammo, depending on the size and type of the projectile.

You can craft manually at this Ammo Workbench, but you can mass-produce ammo far more efficiently with Create's Sequenced Assembly. (Except shotgun shells, grenades, and rockets)
ze.quest.172.title: The Tail Wagging the Dog
ze.quest.172.subtitle: Attachment Workbench
ze.quest.172.des: Most gun attachments can be crafted at this workbench.
ze.quest.173.title: A Gen Z Essential
ze.quest.173.subtitle: Earmuffs
ze.quest.173.des:
These earmuffs block almost all loud or annoying sounds, and you can block the sounds you want at the Engineer's Workbench.

You can also dye them to look a bit cooler.

Combine them with your helmet to make them more useful. Combine the helmet again to detach them.

However, due to a bug in the mod itself, the earmuffs fail to block some noises. Using Extreme Sound Muffler is recommended. Click the speaker icon in your inventory or press the hotkey (Numpad /) to mute the sounds you want.
ze.quest.174.title: Portable Battery
ze.quest.174.subtitle: Capacitor
ze.quest.174.des:
The Create Crafts & Additions Accumulator can store electricity, but when you pick it up, its internal power is lost.

This capacitor keeps its internal power intact even when picked up. Right-click with the Engineer's Hammer to set the input/output of that face.

The tier determines how much power it can hold.
ze.quest.175.title: Geologist
ze.quest.175.subtitle: Prospecting Tool and Core Sampling Drill
ze.quest.175.des:
There are countless veins you haven't discovered. To find them, you need a Prospecting Tool.
Veins exist per chunk (F3+G), and some chunks may have no veins at all.

Hold right-click with the Prospecting Tool on the ground to find the approximate location of veins in that chunk or nearby chunks.

Once you've roughly worked out where a vein is, you can get its exact info with the Core Sampling Drill in that chunk.
