Charge the drill with power and right-click, and the drill takes a cross-section sample of that chunk. When it's done, right-click to collect the sample and check what components that vein contains. You can look up vein info by searching for veins in the Engineer's Manual.

Now that you've found a vein, in the next quest you can craft a machine that mines minerals from the vein.
ze.quest.176.title: Infinite Mining
ze.quest.176.subtitle: Excavator
ze.quest.176.des:
Set it up in a chunk with a vein and supply power, and the Excavator digs out some of the surrounding ground and then begins mining the vein. The mined output is discharged from the port on the back of the machine.

You can get those minerals from this vein infinitely. In exchange, it consumes a lot of power.

For how to craft it, check the Engineer's Manual or search for the Excavator.
ze.quest.177.title: Overkill Begins
ze.quest.177.subtitle: Extreme Crafting Table
ze.quest.177.des:
With the transcendent engineering parts provided by the Galactic Federation, you can enter a technology even more transcendent than theirs, one that perhaps only you in the universe can reach. But once you consume the transcendent engineering parts, you can no longer get the Galactic Federation's support to escape the Overworld.

Surround the crafting table compressed from 81 crafting tables with the transcendent engineering parts, antimatter, and Crystal Matrix Ingots made of Nether Stars and diamonds to craft the Extreme Crafting Table.

The Extreme Crafting Table supports 9*9 recipes, and sadly it can't do the job of a regular crafting table.
ze.quest.178.title: Dust to Dust
ze.quest.178.subtitle: Neutron Collector
ze.quest.178.des:
Collects neutron particles floating in the air so you can obtain Neutron Piles.

To make proper use of Neutron Piles, you'll probably need to set up several of these machines.
ze.quest.179.title: Density Overload
ze.quest.179.subtitle: Neutronium Compressor
ze.quest.179.des: Unlike the regular Matter Condenser, it compresses a single specific element and needs no separate storage medium.
ze.quest.180.title: The Power of the Universe in My Hands
ze.quest.180.subtitle: Infinity Ingot
ze.quest.180.des:
Combine a Neutronium Ingot with the Infinity Catalyst and Crystal Matrix containing everything to craft an Infinity Ingot.

With this ingot you can craft the strongest weapons, gear, and armor.
ze.quest.181.title: Indulging Myself
ze.quest.181.subtitle: Robot Core
ze.quest.181.des:
Process an Infinity Ingot, antimatter, and a Teleportation Core to craft a Robot Core.

You can build a pretty robot based on this Robot Core.

Right-click the robot with an empty hand to command it to follow you or to wait. Then hold the items described below and right-click to see which commands they give.

The oak button lets you choose whether to receive notifications about the robot's status.
The book lets you check the robot's current status.
The book and quill lets you check the robot's enchantment status.
Dye paints the robot in that color.

When the robot kills enemies, it gains experience and levels up. Enchantments are applied accordingly, and the robot becomes even stronger.
ze.quest.182.title: 81-Inch Monitor
ze.quest.182.subtitle: Extreme Crafting Terminal
ze.quest.182.des: A terminal that lets you use the Extreme Crafting Table from the AE system.
ze.quest.183.title: World Geography
ze.quest.183.subtitle: Nature's Compass
ze.quest.183.des: A compass that tells you the location of the biome you want.
ze.quest.184.title: Hell
ze.quest.184.subtitle: The Nether
ze.quest.184.des:
The Nether, the world deep beneath this world (the Overworld), is a hellish realm made of lava and stone that burns forever.

The usual way to get there is to open a portal framed with obsidian, but if you're short on resources, you can also get there through the pull of the dimension.

Stay at a Y coordinate below -60 and the dimension's power will slowly drag you in.
To return, do the reverse: stay at the highest Y coordinate in the Nether and you'll come back.
ze.quest.185.title: The Road to the End
ze.quest.185.subtitle: Eye of Ender
ze.quest.185.des:
Explore this world (the Overworld) and you'll find traces of a fairly advanced civilization. For some reason, most of it is now in ruins.

To find the cause, you need to obtain an eye that will guide you to the source of it all.

You may be able to get an eye from some high-ranking villagers or powerful beings. Or you can craft one yourself. Or, if all else fails, you might get one out of a chest by sheer luck.
ze.quest.186.title: Ruins Leading to the End
ze.quest.186.subtitle: Stronghold
ze.quest.186.des:
Throw the eye and it will follow its instincts, leading you to the source of it all. It's a secret place buried deep underground, so once you've roughly arrived, you may have to dig down to sneak in.

Once there, you'll have to activate devices to push forward through the stronghold, a vast labyrinth. But who knows what has corrupted it, a horde of monsters will block your way.
ze.quest.187.title: Into the Void
ze.quest.187.subtitle: The End
ze.quest.187.des: After many expeditions, you've gathered all the eyes to put in the portal. You slotted the eyes into the portal frame to open the portal. With everything ready, you jumped into the portal and arrived in the End.
ze.quest.188.title: Assemble
ze.quest.188.subtitle: Town Hall and Build Tool
ze.quest.188.des:
You've found it hard to survive alone in this world. Horrible monsters lurk in the dark, the big-nosed tribesfolk demand nothing but emeralds, and the ones who seem like they might actually be reasonable are hostile to you.

In such an environment, you decide to found a colony, hoping there are others like you out there.

Craft a Town Hall block yourself, or right-click the Town Hall in an abandoned town hall building. If you crafted the Town Hall block, decide your community's architectural style with the Build Tool and name the colony with the Town Hall block, announcing yourself to this world and rallying the remaining survivors.

The Build Tool is explained on the next page.
ze.quest.188.des2:
While holding the blocks for the building you want to construct, right-click the ground with the Build Tool to open the UI.

Next, select Switch Pack and scroll down to choose the architectural style of the faction you'll build.
After selecting your preferred style, choose Fundamentals among the structure categories at the bottom center, then select the Town Hall. Press the button on the left of the UI to preview how the structure will be built at each stage.
Press ESC to close the UI briefly and see how the building will be placed. When you're done checking, or if you need adjustments, right-click with the Build Tool again, adjust the structure with the arrow buttons on the right, and press the green check icon at the bottom center to confirm.
ze.quest.188.des3:
You can't build the Town Hall right away. Check the next quest.

By the way, summoning the Wither is restricted inside a colony.
ze.quest.189.title: Skulleton
ze.quest.189.subtitle: Flaming Skull Sword
ze.quest.189.des:
To get lots of Nether Stars from now on, you'll need plenty of Wither Skeleton Skulls.

The Flaming Skull Sword is a weapon whose powerful cutting and flames guarantee Wither Skeleton Skulls even from regular Skeletons.
ze.quest.190.title: Blacksmith of the Cosmos
ze.quest.190.subtitle: Infinity Weapons and Tools
ze.quest.190.des:
With Infinity Ingots, you can craft the strongest weapons and tools.

The Sword of the Cosmos can kill every creature it slashes in one hit.
The Longbow of the Heavens fires faster than a regular bow, and when an arrow hits a block, it summons a rain of arrows from the sky that deals wide-area damage.
The World Breaker can instantly break every block, including bedrock, and carries the luck of the cosmos. Also, right-click while sneaking to switch it into hammer form, and mining a block then mines a wide area of blocks at once.
The Planet Eater can instantly dig dirt-type blocks, and just like the World Breaker, right-click while sneaking to switch to Black Hole mode and scoop up a wide area of dirt-type blocks at once.
The Ruin of Nature instantly breaks trees, and right-click while sneaking to destroy all plants around you.
The Hoe of the Blue Earth tills a wide area at once when you right-click dirt, and right-clicking crops or saplings makes them grow quickly.

If you break blocks with a tool that can destroy a wide area, like the World Breaker or Planet Eater, the drops of the broken blocks are packed into a single item as compressed matter, and right-clicking it while holding it releases all the contents.
ze.quest.191.title: Wrap Me in the Cosmos
ze.quest.191.subtitle: Infinity Set
ze.quest.191.des:
Once you're wearing this armor, there's almost nothing left to fear.

The Infinity Helmet keeps the wearer's hunger full and grants Night Vision.
The Infinity Chestplate spreads wings so the wearer can fly, and prevents fall damage. It also blocks all debuffs.
The Infinity Leggings keep the wearer from 'continuously' burning.
The Infinity Boots raise the wearer's jump height by 4 blocks and make movement extremely fast. They also automatically step up one-block-high blocks.

In addition, when you wear the full set, it protects the wearer from radiation.
ze.quest.192.title: Higher-Dimensional Chest
ze.quest.192.subtitle: Infinity Chest
ze.quest.192.des:
It can hold a huge variety of item types, and each slot holds nearly unlimited quantities (about 2 billion) instead of 64.

The contents are preserved even when it's destroyed.
ze.quest.193.title: Gravity Machine
ze.quest.193.subtitle: Gyrodyne
ze.quest.193.des:
There are a few ways to fly. One is riding a Gyrodyne.

This aircraft needs no fuel and flies purely on your own strength (hunger). After boarding, press W to build up speed, and once you've got some speed, you can control altitude with the jump and sneak keys and move with WASD.

Press Ctrl to dismount, and if the aircraft is damaged, right-click while sneaking to repair it by spending hunger.
ze.quest.194.title: Take to the Skies
ze.quest.194.subtitle: Immersive Aircraft
ze.quest.194.des:
Have you tried the Gyrodyne? If you have, you know that something that drains hunger and is that slow is embarrassing to even call an aircraft. Luckily, you can now craft high-performance aircraft with engines using Blaze Burners.

For the Airship and Quadrocopter, control altitude with the jump and sneak keys and move horizontally with WASD.
For the Biplane, press the jump key to start the engine and raise the propeller speed. The sneak key does the opposite and turns off the engine. Once the biplane has speed, press S to climb and W to descend. A and D turn left and right.

To dismount any aircraft, press Ctrl, and to repair, right-click while sneaking to spend hunger on repairs. You can also install extra parts to modify them, and for airships, you can craft the Cargo Airship and Warship through crafting.

Besides the aircraft required, a variety of other aircraft are available. Search '@civilian_aviation' in EMI (the panel at the bottom of the inventory) to check them out.
ze.quest.195.title: Set the Table
ze.quest.195.subtitle: Farmer's Delight
ze.quest.195.des:
First, I should explain why you need to actually prepare meals. Otherwise you'll just say 'ugh, too much effort' and eat a carrot with gold plated on it.
If there were only the hunger and saturation system, that'd be the right answer, but here it's a different story.

First, every food has nutrients. Open the diet tab (hunger icon) in your inventory to see the nutrients you've eaten. Fill them past a certain level and you'll get several nice buffs. Eating only veggies won't cut it, right? Also, these nutrients reset when you die, so now you've got a reason not to die. (However, if your sugar level gets too high, you'll suffer from constant hunger.)

Second, trying many different kinds of food increases your max health. You can see the foods you've tried and haven't tried in the book you'll get as a reward. This doesn't reset when you die. But it's a good reason to try cooking lots of dishes, right?

The cooking equipment is explained on the next page.
ze.quest.195.des2:
The Stove can cook food like a campfire, and is a good heat source for a Cooking Pot or Skillet placed on top.

The Cooking Pot is placed on top of a Stove and lets you cook various foods by boiling them with water.

The Skillet cooks when you hold it in your main hand in front of a Stove, hold the food to cook in your other hand, and keep holding right-click. You can also right-click while sneaking to place it and use it. Or you can swing it at the people you don't like. (Sadly, it doesn't block bullets.)

The Cutting Board is used with a knife to prep or slice food. Also... you can do other things with a cutting board. For example, put a log on it and strip the bark with an axe...
ze.quest.196.title: Checking Quests
ze.quest.196.subtitle: PDA
ze.quest.196.des:
With the PDA in your hand, you can check how to survive from here on. It also tells you what you can do at your current skill level.

Even without the PDA, you can press L to see this screen.
ze.quest.197.title: Get Out of the Courtyard
ze.quest.197.subtitle: Naga Courtyard
ze.quest.197.des:
Using the Empty Magic Map you got as the previous quest reward, you can learn the terrain of this forest world, its powerful monsters, and where they were found.

Most places repel visitors with magic, so it's important to find the Naga Courtyard, the only place without a protective spell.

A monster guarding the courtyard is waiting for you there.
ze.quest.198.title: How Do I Naga Out
ze.quest.198.subtitle: Naga
ze.quest.198.des:
The Naga, which takes the form of a giant serpent, circles around you and then charges at you. If you block its charge with a shield, the Naga is stunned, giving you an opening to attack. When the Naga's health is low, its tail gets progressively shorter.

Once you obtain Naga Scales, you'll be able to break through the magic barrier of the nearby Lich Tower.

Also, if you right-click the chest created when the Naga dies with the Magic Map, the map marks that region's Naga as defeated. You can mark other bosses the same way.
ze.quest.199.title: The Magic Castle
ze.quest.199.subtitle: Lich Tower
ze.quest.199.des:
With the Naga's scales, you can break through the Lich Tower's magic barrier. The entrance is sealed, so you have to break through the wall with a pickaxe to get in.

True to its master's nature, undead monsters and magical creatures will try to stop you in the tower. Survive the attacks and reach the top of the tower.
ze.quest.200.title: Forced Ascension (Not Optional)
ze.quest.200.subtitle: Lich
ze.quest.200.des:
You can have an audience with the Lich at the top of the tower. Audience, my foot, you're the one who stormed in, so it will attack you on sight.

The Lich will attack you with various spells, while shielding itself with a magic barrier to block your attacks.

To break through the Lich's shield, you have to bat back the spells its clones fire so they hit the Lich. Do that and the shield takes damage and gradually shatters.

Defeat the Lich and the curses it cast over various biomes will be lifted.
ze.quest.201.title: Resting Place of the Knights
ze.quest.201.subtitle: Dark Forest Ruins
ze.quest.201.des:
With the curse over the Dark Forest lifted, you can now reach the Dark Forest ruins. The ruins are underground, so you must find the entrance and open it.

To open the entrance, place any trophy on the trophy pedestal near the entrance to prove you're worthy of entering the Knights' resting place.

The resting place is shaped like a maze. Find your way with the Maze Map you'll get as a reward. The maze's floors are intricately intertwined, so you may need a lot of maps. They may run short, so use them sparingly. And the goblins guarding the knights' rest will try to stop you.

Beyond a door double-blocked by iron bars with an obsidian border between them, in the room you can awaken the eternal sleep of the gods' knights of the past.
ze.quest.202.title: Knights of the Gods
ze.quest.202.subtitle: Knight Phantom(s)
ze.quest.202.des:
If you've reached the place where they rest, they will fend off intruders. Maybe they're trying to test you.

There are six of them, normally just armor and weapons floating around, but when it's time to attack you, they'll reveal their forms.

Defeat them and they'll acknowledge you, and the Carminite devices of the Dark Tower will obey your commands.
ze.quest.203.title: Carminite Tower
ze.quest.203.subtitle: Dark Tower
ze.quest.203.des:
Having earned the knights' approval, you're now qualified to enter the Dark Tower. You must climb the tower by activating its Carminite devices, defeating the golems and ghasts that get in your way. (Most people just can't be bothered and climb by stacking blocks or the like.)

At the top of the tower, the first Ghast awaits you.
ze.quest.204.title: The First Ghast
ze.quest.204.subtitle: Ur-Ghast
ze.quest.204.des:
True to the title of the first Ghast, the Ur-Ghast is enormous and has a very annoying strategy.

While you're facing off against the Ur-Ghast, lightning will strike random spots in the four rooms connected to the top floor, and Ghast Spawns (Mini Ghasts) will be summoned there. Deal with the Mini Ghasts there and the Ghast Trap in the center of the room will charge; give the charged trap a redstone signal and it will activate, pulling the Ur-Ghast toward it and into melee range (the Ur-Ghast must be nearby, and if it's casting a particular attack, this is ignored). That's your window to attack.

When low on health, the Ur-Ghast sheds tears that rapidly wear down the durability of the head armor of whoever they hit, so be careful.

Defeat the Ur-Ghast and you can obtain the Fiery Tears, the Ur-Ghast's burning tears.
ze.quest.205.title: Your Classic Maze Dungeon
ze.quest.205.subtitle: Labyrinth
ze.quest.205.des:
With the poisonous mosquitoes in the swamp extinct, you can now reach the Labyrinth in the swamp. The Labyrinth lies beneath a hill, and a variety of bug-like monsters and Minotaurs will greet you. To avoid getting lost in the maze-like Labyrinth, I recommend charting your path with the Maze Map you'll get as a reward. If you run short of maps, you can craft more.

The Labyrinth's maze has two floors in total, and to descend to the next floor, you need to find the room where an iron grate blocks the passage connected below. Once you reach the next floor, you'll need a new Maze Map.

As you explore, you'll reach the Minoshroom's room, which is blocked off with oak fences.
ze.quest.206.title: Minotaur Musume: Pretty Maze
ze.quest.206.subtitle: Minoshroom
ze.quest.206.des: The Minoshroom has low intelligence and does nothing but charge attacks, so you'll have plenty of openings. Eat the Meef Stroganoff you get from defeating it, and you'll be able to endure the scorching heat at the heart of the swamp.
ze.quest.207.title: Predator of the Swamp
ze.quest.207.subtitle: Hydra Lair
ze.quest.207.des: In the middle of the swamp, with a big hill at its back, the dragon Hydra hunts the animals around it.
ze.quest.208.title: Cut off one head, and two more shall take its place.
ze.quest.208.subtitle: Hydra
ze.quest.208.des:
The three-headed dragon, the Hydra, sets creatures ablaze by shooting scorching breath from its mouth. It also launches fireballs or sometimes bites directly with its huge jaws.

To deal effective damage to the Hydra, you have to bat the fireballs back so they hit its head. Black smoke appears around the head that's about to fire a fireball, so spot it and get ready to deflect the fireball.

Since the Hydra mostly uses fire attacks, preparing something like Fire Resistance potions lets you beat it relatively safely.

Defeat the Hydra and you can obtain Fiery Blood, the Hydra's burning blood. You can also get Hydra Chops, which make good food.
ze.quest.209.title: Make Way, the Alpha Yeti of the Snowy Forest Cave Is Coming Through
ze.quest.209.subtitle: Yeti Cave
ze.quest.209.des:
The cold of the Snowy Forest has eased somewhat, so you can now enter the Yeti Cave.

Yetis live beneath the square hill. They definitely won't be welcoming you, at least.
ze.quest.210.title: Alpha Yeti
ze.quest.210.subtitle: Alpha Yeti
ze.quest.210.des:
The Alpha Yeti, the big boy among yetis, will attack you to protect the yetis from outside creatures.

It drops icicles from the ceiling, throws ice bombs, and can even pick you up and throw you.

The Alpha Yeti attacks with all its might, and if you drag things out, it sometimes gets exhausted and collapses. That's your chance. Hearing this, it might sound easy to deal with, but the yetis won't want to see their boss get beaten.

With the Alpha Yeti Fur you get from defeating it, you can withstand the cold of the Glacier in the heart of the Snowy Forest and have an audience with the Snow Queen at the Aurora Palace.
ze.quest.211.title: Let It Go
ze.quest.211.subtitle: Aurora Palace
ze.quest.211.des:
Climb the Glacier, a high icy area in the middle of the Snowy Forest, and you'll find cute penguins and the Aurora Palace standing at its center.

The Snow Queen sits on the top floor of the Aurora Palace, and her minions below will try to stop you. Run across the slippery ice and make your way to the top. If you find a spot where the ceiling is sealed with ice, that's a sign the Snow Queen is right above it.
ze.quest.212.title: Never Gonna Give You Up
ze.quest.212.subtitle: Snow Queen
ze.quest.212.des:
Having barely made it to the top floor of the palace, you can now have an audience with the Snow Queen... Just like the Lich, she is hostile to you.

She rides on the ice and flies around, blocking your attacks. Your chance comes whenever she lands on the floor after a slam attack.
ze.quest.213.title: Deep in the Cave
ze.quest.213.subtitle: Troll Cave
ze.quest.213.des:
Once you defeat the Hydra, Ur-Ghast, and Snow Queen, the acid rain falling on the Highlands stops and you can enter. However, the thorn thicket at its center blocks any further entry, so you'll have to solve that around the Highlands.

The Troll Cave is deep underground, reached by a cave in the Highlands or under the giant cloud. At its center is a giant obsidian, and around the edges are ordinary obsidian piles.

You can't mine the giant obsidian with your current gear, so mine the regular obsidian piles and grab the magic beans from the chest in the center. The trolls don't seem too happy to see you, though.
ze.quest.214.title: Steve and the Beanstalk
ze.quest.214.subtitle: Magic Beans
ze.quest.214.des:
The Magic Beans seem to be a special crop, judging by how preciously the trolls guard them. To find out, you'll need to head back up to the surface.

Take the Magic Beans to the area under the giant cloud and you'll see some glittering high-quality soil. Plant the beans there, and with a loud rumble they will grow fast and huge, all the way up to the giant cloud.

If you think about the fairy tale, you know there's good treasure up there. Go climb it.
ze.quest.215.title: Steve's Travels
ze.quest.215.subtitle: Cabin in the Clouds
ze.quest.215.des: Up in the clouds you'll see a huge cabin and a tree. And two giants too. According to the fairy tale, you know you have to take those giants down.
ze.quest.216.title: Right Block, Dang Big Pickaxe
ze.quest.216.subtitle: Giant
ze.quest.216.des:
The two giants don't seem happy about your intrusion. Come to think of it, hardly anyone has ever welcomed you warmly.

Anyway, defeat both giants and the Giant Miner will drop a Giant's Pickaxe. It's a stone pickaxe, but I have no doubt it can mine giant obsidian.
ze.quest.217.title: Where's the Genie?
ze.quest.217.subtitle: Lamp of Cinders
ze.quest.217.des:
Take the Giant's Pickaxe, mine the giant obsidian in the Troll Cave, and you'll get the Lamp of Cinders from the chest in the center.

Hold right-click in the air with the Lamp of Cinders and then release, and it will instantly burn the surrounding thorns to ashes.

That means the path to the final destination has finally opened.
ze.quest.218.title: Half-Forest 3
ze.quest.218.subtitle: Final Castle
ze.quest.218.des: Burning through the thorns, you reach the center of the Highlands and arrive at the Final Castle. When you reach its center...
ze.quest.219.title: Totem of Undying (Mass-Produced)
ze.quest.219.subtitle: Charm of Life
ze.quest.219.des:
You can find these in chests in some dungeons in the Twilight Forest. While it's in your inventory, it works like a Totem of Undying: it is consumed when the holder is about to die, giving them a chance to survive.

You can combine four tier 1 charms to make a tier 2 charm. When used, a tier 2 charm gives the holder several buffs that help with survival.
ze.quest.220.title: /gamerule keepInventory true
ze.quest.220.subtitle: Charm of Keeping
ze.quest.220.des:
You can find these in chests in some dungeons in the Twilight Forest, or from Maze Slimes. If you die and respawn while carrying one in your inventory, it preserves some of the items you were carrying, depending on the charm's tier.

A tier 1 charm keeps the item in your hand and your equipped armor, tier 2 adds your entire hotbar, and tier 3 keeps your whole inventory.
ze.quest.221.title: Colorful
ze.quest.221.subtitle: Quest Ram
ze.quest.221.des:
Find the Quest Ram living in a certain temple in the Enchanted Forest and give it wool of every color, and it will give you a reward.

Some colors of wool can be obtained from a hidden dispenser in the temple.
ze.quest.222.title: First Hire
ze.quest.222.subtitle: Builder's Hut
ze.quest.222.des:
To build your colony's buildings, you need to hire a builder. And to hire a builder, you need a builder's hut.

While holding the Builder's Hut block, you can build it with the build tool just like the Town Hall (make sure it doesn't overlap with the Town Hall building).

Once the Builder's Hut block is placed, right-click it to open the UI and press Manage Workers to hire a citizen gathered nearby. The skills required for a builder are highlighted.

After hiring, go back, press Building Settings, check the required materials, then press Build Building, and the hired builder will check the job and carry it out.

You can find the required materials by asking the builder directly or by clicking the Required Resources tab on the left of the Builder's Hut block, and you can also check them remotely with the Resource Scroll you get as a reward. Put the materials in the builder's inventory or the Builder's Hut block's storage.

While you wait for construction to finish, read the next page.
ze.quest.222.des2:
The tier of a facility determines the grade of tools its workers can use. At first they can only use wood and gold tools, but after upgrading they can use iron, diamond, Netherite, and even enchanted tools.

Citizens, workers included, need to sleep at night and won't work when it rains. Also, if a citizen dies in the colony, everyone stops working for a day of mourning.

Like you, citizens constantly lose hunger and need a steady food supply. They can also catch diseases and can be killed by monsters nearby. For now you have to handle all of that yourself, but by continuing to build the necessary buildings and hire workers, you can stabilize the colony.

If there's an icon above a citizen, it means they have something to say to you. Become a great leader!
ze.quest.223.title: Recruiting Outsiders
ze.quest.223.subtitle: Tavern
ze.quest.223.des:
You can't just make your citizens sleep on the streets, so build a tavern to provide temporary lodging.

The tavern has a total of 4 beds, enough for all the citizens recruited early on. Once all citizens are lying in bed, you'll get a chat notification. If you sleep through the night before that, the discontent of citizens who couldn't get a bed will grow.

You can only build one per colony, but it also serves to recruit outsiders with great stats.

To recruit an outsider, you need a spare residence and must provide the items they ask for.

If an outsider dies in the colony, your colony's reputation for safety drops, and outsiders will take longer to show up.
ze.quest.224.title: You. Apply to Grad School.
ze.quest.224.subtitle: University
ze.quest.224.des:
To improve the overall abilities of colony residents or to build more advanced buildings, research at the University is essential.

You can hire researchers to carry out the research you want, as long as you meet the research requirements.
ze.quest.225.title: Buying Your Own Home
ze.quest.225.subtitle: Residence
ze.quest.225.des:
Citizens aren't satisfied with beds at the tavern, so you'll eventually have to build them homes.

The first-tier building can only house one person, but you can increase the capacity by upgrading.

If a man and a woman live in the same residence (the tavern included) and there's one spot left, they'll have a child. You can decide whether to allow this in the Town Hall block's settings (it's allowed by default).
ze.quest.226.title: Neighborhood Watch Commandos
ze.quest.226.subtitle: Guard Tower
ze.quest.226.des:
Once your colony reaches a decent size, it becomes a target for hostile forces nearby. Citizens will be afraid and sometimes demand that you build a guard tower.

Hired guards patrol the surrounding buildings. They are mainly active at night and sleep during the day. They live in the guard tower, so they don't need separate housing.
ze.quest.227.title: Soup Kitchen
ze.quest.227.subtitle: Restaurant
ze.quest.227.des:
If handing out food to citizens one by one is too much, build a restaurant. If the restaurant has food, citizens will go there first.

Waiters serve food to citizens and can do basic cooking (smelting). To serve more complex dishes, build a Cook's Kitchen.

Choose the food the restaurant will serve and supply the ingredients.
ze.quest.228.title: Say it! I am an idiot sandwich!
ze.quest.228.subtitle: Cook's Kitchen
ze.quest.228.des:
To serve citizens high-quality food, you need to hire a cook at the Cook's Kitchen.

Cooks can make many dishes, including some that you can't cook yourself.
ze.quest.229.title: Gone Fishin'
ze.quest.229.subtitle: Fisher's Hut
ze.quest.229.des:
The hired fisher takes the fishing rod they're given and fishes in a 7*7 area of nearby water (it depends on the building style, but usually when you build a fisher's hut, a fishing spot comes as a bonus).

They mostly catch fish, but they can also fish up treasure.
ze.quest.230.title: Amazon Fulfillment Center
ze.quest.230.subtitle: Warehouse and Courier's Hut
ze.quest.230.des:
It stores large quantities of goods for each facility in the colony. Using the Courier's Hut block inside, you can build an additional courier's hut and hire couriers.

Couriers carry goods between facilities. They deliver items requested by a facility's workers, and you can also set a minimum stock on each facility block so couriers won't take those items away, or so they refill them when running low.
ze.quest.231.title: Villager Auto-Farming
ze.quest.231.subtitle: Farm
ze.quest.231.des:
Hire a farmer to grow and harvest various crops.

Place a field (scarecrow) to designate the area where crops will be grown, and the farmer will farm there (it depends on the building style, but usually when you build a farm, a farming area comes as a bonus).
ze.quest.232.title: No Bread? Guess We Starve
ze.quest.232.subtitle: Bakery
ze.quest.232.des: This is where the hired baker bakes, mainly making bread, cookies, and pies.
ze.quest.233.title: Deforestation Inc.
ze.quest.233.subtitle: Lumberjack's Hut
ze.quest.233.des:
Give the lumberjack an axe and a hoe, and they can chop trees in the surrounding area or in a region you designate.

They can also do some wood-related processing. For example, you can have them strip bark off trees.

You can also hire a fruit grower to harvest tree fruits.
ze.quest.234.title: Into the Deep
ze.quest.234.subtitle: Mine
ze.quest.234.des:
The mine is a facility where you hire miners and give them pickaxes and various supplies to obtain underground resources.

Since it involves digging underground, there are more things to look after than with most facilities. You'll build a platform for miners to go up and down between the surface and the mine and place torches, but if a cave or dungeon is discovered, monsters will go after the miners, so you also need to assign guards.
ze.quest.235.title: Player Interference
ze.quest.235.subtitle: Delivery Chest and Pickup Chest
ze.quest.235.des:
If your colony has a warehouse and a hired courier, there are blocks you can use.

If you put items in a Delivery Chest, the courier moves the items in it to the warehouse and they're used as colony resources.

For a Pickup Chest, set the items you want and the courier will transport those items from the warehouse to the Pickup Chest.

With these, you can supply goods from automation facilities you've already built, and conversely, you can have your colony's surplus resources delivered to you automatically.
ze.quest.236.title: Respawn Point
ze.quest.236.subtitle: Hospital
ze.quest.236.des:
It's a hassle to go look after citizens one by one every time they get sick. To solve this, you need to research the hospital at the University (Vigor research in the Citizen tab).

Build a hospital and hire a doctor so that sick citizens can go to the doctor for treatment. As a side note, even without a doctor, sick citizens will rest at the hospital.
ze.quest.237.title: Cyberpunk 1201
ze.quest.237.subtitle: CyberWare
ze.quest.237.des:
You've probably seen monsters with parts of their bodies replaced by machinery. These are the monsters with the "Cyber" prefix. Maybe someone captured and modified them, or maybe a modified person turned into a zombie... Anyway, you now have a chance to extract their mechanical parts (cyberware) and try them out.

Be careful. Unlike ordinary monsters, they are dangerous beings with various abilities. Let your guard down and they'll turn you into a slab of meat in no time.

At the Cyberware Workbench, you can disassemble extracted cyberware for a low chance to draw a blueprint on paper. The components you get differ depending on the type of cyberware, and the chance of getting a blueprint is low, around 15%%.
ze.quest.238.title: Look Closely
ze.quest.238.subtitle: Scanner
ze.quest.238.des:
To get a blueprint from the Cyberware Workbench, you have to rely on a low chance.

Using the Scanner, you can get that cyberware's blueprint with a high chance. However, scanning takes a long time.

The Cyber Eye used as an ingredient can be used whether it was extracted or crafted.

Cyberware used in the Scanner is always destroyed, and there is a 50%% chance it gets destroyed without giving you a blueprint.
ze.quest.239.title: Cyber Storage (Nothing Special)
ze.quest.239.subtitle: Blueprint Archive and Component Box
ze.quest.239.des:
If you place the Blueprint Archive and Component Box next to the Cyberware Workbench, you can take out their contents and use them directly from the Cyberware Workbench.

The Component Box is portable, and to place it you have to right-click while sneaking.
ze.quest.240.title: Katana Runner
ze.quest.240.subtitle: Katana
ze.quest.240.des:
You've figured out a more efficient way to extract cyberware from cyber monsters.

Attach components to an iron sword to turn it into a katana, and killing cyber monsters with the katana gives a higher chance of getting cyberware. It can take the enchantments that a basic sword can.
ze.quest.241.title: Doc, What Do You Mean "Experimental"?!
ze.quest.241.subtitle: Robosurgeon and Surgery Chamber
ze.quest.241.des:
To install cyberware you've extracted or crafted, you need a Surgery Chamber and a Robosurgeon.

Place the Robosurgeon on top of the Surgery Chamber, use the Robosurgeon to choose which body part to install or remove cyberware from, then step into the Surgery Chamber and close the door, and the surgery begins. Some of your health is drained during this, so if you don't want to die, heal up beforehand.

You can implant extracted cyberware as is, but compared to crafted cyberware it tends to have worse power efficiency or performance, so it's best to use cyberware you crafted yourself whenever possible.

Also, if you're using an old-format skin, you may get kicked. Be careful.
ze.quest.241.des2:
Some cyberware must be installed by removing the original body part and replacing it. A word of caution: if you don't choose a replacement when removing a perfectly healthy part, you'll run into problems. For example, if you remove your heart or brain, you die instantly as soon as the surgery ends. If you remove your stomach, you can't eat, and without an arm or leg you'll be restricted in using items and breaking blocks, or unable to move at all. Fortunately, the Robosurgeon warns you about this in advance with notices or warnings.

Installing cyberware reduces your Essence. You can see this on the bar on the left of the Robosurgeon. You're fine as long as the reduction stays within the blue gauge, but once the red part starts to be reduced, your body begins to reject the cyberware. At that point, you can temporarily relieve the symptoms with a drug called Neuropozyne.

Some cyberware requires power. In that case, you have to install cyberware with power generation or battery cyberware and keep it charged.
ze.quest.242.title: Cyborg-Only Charger
ze.quest.242.subtitle: Charger
ze.quest.242.des: When you stand on it, it syncs with the charger and charges the battery cyberware you have installed. By right-clicking, you can also do the reverse and draw the power from your battery into the charger.
ze.quest.243.title: Proof That Steve Has a Heart
ze.quest.243.subtitle: Creative Battery
ze.quest.243.des: With a Robot Core, you can craft cyberware that produces infinite power.
ze.quest.244.title: Going Live
ze.quest.244.subtitle: Radio Kit
ze.quest.244.des: Once placed, it lures cyber monsters within 64 blocks toward it, making it easier to collect cyberware.
ze.quest.245.title: Brown Belt
ze.quest.245.subtitle: Tool Belt
ze.quest.245.des:
Wear it in the belt slot and hold F to store or take out tools.

To increase its capacity, work it in an anvil together with a Belt Pouch.
ze.quest.246.title: Round and Round
ze.quest.246.subtitle: Millstone
ze.quest.246.des:
You can operate it by connecting power to this machine's cogwheel or the shaft at its bottom.

It mainly grinds ordinary items. To grind types of stone, you'll need something bigger.
ze.quest.247.title: One of the Reasons Behind the Luddite Movement
ze.quest.247.subtitle: Mechanical Arm
ze.quest.247.des:
Before placing it, right-click while sneaking to set the input and output positions.

Once you've set them, placed it, and supplied power, the Mechanical Arm will pick up items from the input and place them at the output.

It can't put items into or take items out of chests and the like directly, so you'll need to use item holders, funnels, belts, and so on.
ze.quest.248.title: That's Speed, Not Velocity
ze.quest.248.subtitle: Rotation Speed Controller
ze.quest.248.des:
If you're sick of fiddling with speed by wiring big and small cogwheels together in a complicated mess, I recommend this machine. Feed rotational force to the shaft, attach a large cogwheel on top, then hold right-click on the part with the numbers to adjust to the speed you want.

Still, speed remains inversely proportional to stress. If you want ultra-high speed, you need to produce a correspondingly generous amount of stress capacity.
ze.quest.249.title: Dragon Slayer
ze.quest.249.subtitle: Ender Dragon
ze.quest.249.des:
Arriving at the center of the End, also called the Void world, you spot a structure in the middle of the island. As you approach, an alien power activates the surrounding towers and finally summons the dragon.

The dragon will give everything it has to drive you out of the End. It recovers its strength through the End Crystals on the surrounding towers, so if you plan to take it down, you must destroy the End Crystals on the towers first.
ze.quest.250.title: Citadel of the Guardian
ze.quest.250.subtitle: Ruined Citadel
ze.quest.250.des:
Defeating the dragon lets you leave the central island. A portal that can teleport you far away appears in the void at the edge of the central island.

To find another powerful foe, you can gather resources from the End and craft a Void Eye to guide you.

Follow the eye and you'll arrive at the Ruined Citadel. Or you could just explore and find it yourself.
ze.quest.251.title: Big Shoulders Bro
ze.quest.251.subtitle: Ender Golem
ze.quest.251.des:
This golem guarding the citadel detects you as an intruder and attacks.

It isn't too hard to kill, but that's proof the citadel's true master is someone else.
ze.quest.252.title: The Face Behind the Mask
ze.quest.252.subtitle: Ender Guardian
ze.quest.252.des:
The Ender Guardian is on the lowest floor of the citadel. With defense as high as its huge frame suggests, physical attacks barely work, and it chains attacks that ignore your armor, making it a tough enemy.

However, it takes magic damage in full, so you should use that. For example, something like the Void Core you got from the Ender Golem.
ze.quest.253.title: Burning Spirit
ze.quest.253.subtitle: Burning Arena
ze.quest.253.des:
Use the Eye of Flame to find it, or explore on your own, and you'll find the Burning Arena, a huge circular arena structure.

True to its name, it's full of Blazes and lava. You have to overcome them and climb to the upper level.
ze.quest.254.title: Lower Your Guard
ze.quest.254.subtitle: Ignited Revenant
ze.quest.254.des:
Once you've climbed a fair way up the arena, the Ignited Revenant will attack you.

It protects itself with the shields wrapped around its body, so you need to attack around the shields or land a critical hit with an axe (Minecraft only) to break them.
ze.quest.255.title: New Life from the Ashes
ze.quest.255.subtitle: Ignis
ze.quest.255.des:
Offer the Burning Ashes from the Revenant at the Altar of Fire on the upper level, and Ignis, also called the Embodiment of Flame, answers the call. Be careful. Ignis will be far stronger than any enemy you've faced so far.

It blocks your attacks with its giant shield, the Bulwark of the Flame, and can stun you, then swings its giant sword, the Incinerator, to burn you with ruthless attacks. Also, when a target hit by Ignis takes damage, Ignis regains health, and the target is afflicted with a curse that scales with their max health and nearly ignores armor.

To land a hit on Ignis, time it for when it lowers its shield briefly to attack. Magic attacks can also deal damage that ignores the shield. Alternatively, deflect the Abyss Fireball (purple projectile) it throws so it hits the shield, and the shield will break.

Ignis can also destroy part of the arena floor to drop you into the lava beneath it, so prepare Fire Resistance potions and the like.
ze.quest.256.title: Ancient Forge
ze.quest.256.subtitle: Soul Forge
ze.quest.256.des:
You can find the Soul Forge by wandering the Nether or by crafting a Monstrosity Eye and following it.

It seems Ancient Debris was once forged and used here. Otherwise there's no way there'd be this much Ancient Debris around.
ze.quest.257.title: Ancient War Machine
ze.quest.257.subtitle: Netherite Monstrosity
ze.quest.257.des:
The Netherite Monstrosity standing guard deep inside the forge will spot you when you get close and attack.

Living up to its title of ancient war machine, it will launch wide-ranging attacks with its huge body made entirely of Netherite. It also has an attack that rains lava, so prepare Fire Resistance potions and the like.

This giant beast's weak point is its head, so I recommend attacking it directly there or with ranged attacks like arrows or firearms.
ze.quest.258.title: Ancient... Pet Monster
ze.quest.258.subtitle: Netherite Ministrosity
ze.quest.258.des:
The Netherite Ministrosity, found in a hidden spot in the forge, can be activated by attaching the Lava Power Cell you got from defeating the Netherite Monstrosity. If you can't find the hidden spot, you can craft a Netherite Effigy and right-click to summon it.

It regards whoever attached the cell as its owner, so you don't need to fight this little guy.

Its small frame means it has no combat abilities, but it has a 5*3 storage inventory. You can heal it by feeding it coal, and carry it around in a bucket. You can also right-click while sneaking to make it follow you, move it where you want, or have it wait.

When the Netherite Ministrosity dies, it is guaranteed to drop a Netherite Effigy. You can place it to revive it, but you'll need to attach a Lava Power Cell again.
ze.quest.259.title: How to Train Your Dragon (WIP)
ze.quest.259.subtitle: Dragon Egg
ze.quest.259.des:
When you defeat the dragon, a Dragon Egg spawns in the central structure. If you touch it, it teleports to a random spot nearby.

It is affected by gravity, so if there's no block beneath it, it falls. Use this by placing something like a torch underneath, and you can get it as an item.

Not yet, but maybe someday we'll get to see a dragon hatched from this egg?
ze.quest.260.title: For the Latecomers
ze.quest.260.subtitle: End Crystal
ze.quest.260.des:
Someone ahead of you may have already defeated the Ender Dragon. But then latecomers wouldn't be able to clear the quest, would they?

Craft four End Crystals and place them on the four bedrock blocks of the central structure, and the dragon will be summoned again.
ze.quest.261.title: A Knight's Shame
ze.quest.261.subtitle: Steel Knight
ze.quest.261.des:
Found in front of the End Portal room at its base or in the Steel Knight's Chamber, this giant steel knight acts solely to uphold its mission.

When you get close, the knight awakens and swings its huge axe, the Axe of a Thousand, trying to eliminate you. Its steel armor blocks every attack. But it isn't completely invincible. The spot where the sword is stuck in its back is its only weakness. The knight knows this too, so it won't easily leave an opening.

Wait for it to slam its axe down. It will expose itself while pulling the heavy axe back out.
ze.quest.262.title: Made of Stone
ze.quest.262.subtitle: Steel Knight's Chamber
ze.quest.262.des: This chamber, rarely found underground in the Overworld, is guarded by the Steel Knight alone.
ze.quest.263.title: The Nest
ze.quest.263.subtitle: Umvuthana Village
ze.quest.263.des:
The Umvuthana Village, found in the Savanna biome, is a tribal village centered around its chief, Umvuthi, the Sun Chief.

Under normal circumstances they see you as an enemy, and the Umvuthana tribesmen will swarm and attack you, while the chief, Umvuthi, sits on his throne and scorches you with the power of the sun.

If you're lucky enough to get one of their masks and wear it, they'll see you as an ally and won't strike first. However, if you attack them, destroy the village, or take off the mask, they'll attack you without mercy.

While they regard you as friendly, you can offer gold to Umvuthi to receive the Blessing of the Sun, which lets you wield the power of the sun for an extended time. With the blessing, right-click anywhere with an empty hand to use Sunstrike, calling down sunlight from the sky to burn the target. Right-click while sneaking to charge up and fire a powerful beam with Solar Beam.
ze.quest.264.title: Firebird
ze.quest.264.subtitle: Umvuthi, the Sun Chief
ze.quest.264.des:
If you want to take down Umvuthi, the Sun Chief, I recommend preparing thoroughly. He stays seated on his throne, keeps summoning Umvuthana to corner you, and scorches you with the power of the sun.

When his health drops to 75 or below, he summons Umvuthana Cranes. The Umvuthana Cranes stay by his side and pour life force into him, and while this goes on, Umvuthi is invincible. Because of this, if a Umvuthana Crane shows up, it's best to kill it immediately.
ze.quest.265.title: Frost Beast
ze.quest.265.subtitle: Frostmaw
ze.quest.265.des:
This huge beast, found in snowy plains or the Inverted Icicles biome, is usually asleep. If you get near, it pops the Ice Crystal in its hand into its mouth, roars, and starts attacking you.

It has attack power and health to match its massive build, and freezes its target with the Ice Crystal.

There's a bit of a trick. While invisible from something like an Invisibility potion, you can walk up to the sleeping Frostmaw and steal the Ice Crystal from its hand. Of course, the Frostmaw will notice right away that its Ice Crystal was stolen and immediately go looking for the culprit. Better be careful. Even if it's lost its freezing ability, that huge body is still there.
ze.quest.266.title: In Search of Enlightenment
ze.quest.266.subtitle: Sculptor's Monastery
ze.quest.266.des:
This monastery, mostly found in mountainous of forest terrain, was once home to monks who gathered to study the magic of the earth, or the crust. But these days, only spirit monsters called Bluffs guard it.

Only the last monk remains at the center of the monastery: the big, round Sculptor.
ze.quest.267.title: Bluffing
ze.quest.267.subtitle: Bluff
ze.quest.267.des:
These spirits, who have settled in the Sculptor's Monastery, will attack you with terrestrial magic.

Defeat them to obtain Bluff Staves, which let you take the trial of Tongbi the Sculptor, the last remaining monk.
ze.quest.268.title: Ascension
ze.quest.268.subtitle: Terrestrial Gauntlet
ze.quest.268.des:
Talk to Tongbi the Sculptor in the center of the Sculptor's Monastery and hand him a Bluff Staff to begin the trial. The trial is to climb the platforms of earth that Tongbi conjures with terrestrial power, and face him at the top.

Cheating is not allowed in this trial. If you are caught flying or placing or breaking blocks, you fail. Of course, you can hand over another Bluff Staff and try again. Weirdly flexible, though, he seems to let Jump Boost potions slide. Maybe that's because the trial is nearly impossible without one.

Once you finish, Tongbi carves the Terrestrial Gauntlet, a tool that helps you wield terrestrial power, and hands it to you, passing the power of the Terramancers on to you. And then he..
ze.quest.269.title: Wrecking Monk
ze.quest.269.subtitle: Tongbi the Sculptor
ze.quest.269.des:
If you don't feel like taking Tongbi's trial but still want terrestrial power, there's always the option of killing him. Well, I wouldn't recommend it.

When defeated, he drops a random piece of the Terramancer set. But those are all things you can get from the Sculptor's Monastery anyway, so this path is hardly worth it. The fact that he has lived through such long years means he is just that strong.
ze.quest.270.title: Terramancer Master
ze.quest.270.subtitle: Terramancer Set
ze.quest.270.des: This gear, obtainable from the Sculptor's Monastery, is imbued with the power of the Terramancers. Or.. by killing the last remaining monk.
ze.quest.271.title: Lost Technology
ze.quest.271.subtitle: Ancient Factory
ze.quest.271.des:
This factory, deep underground in the Overworld, is hard to find, so you usually locate it by crafting an Eye of the Machine. Crafting that eye requires Create's mechanical processes. With some luck, you might stumble onto it.

Once you step inside, the machines guarding the factory will attack you. To awaken the mighty being here, you will need a Nether Star.
ze.quest.272.title: Cyber Wither
ze.quest.272.subtitle: The Harbinger
ze.quest.272.des:
Implanted with a Nether Star, the Harbinger blasts the blocks around it and starts wiping out every living thing except the machines nearby. Built in the image of the Wither, this ancient war machine ruthlessly fires missiles, lasers, and more to hound its target.

At regular intervals the Harbinger switches attack modes, alternating between missiles and lasers, and its other attacks include a charge, Wither homing missiles, and the Death Laser. Being hit by the Death Laser ignores armor, so it kills its target in an instant.

Luckily, it is a machine, so EMP attacks work on it. Each of the six pillars in the Harbinger's room is fitted with an EMP block, and pulling the lever releases a magnetic pulse that temporarily shuts down most mechanical creatures in range, including the Harbinger. EMP blocks are single-use, but they can be recharged by the Death Lasers of the Harbinger or the Wanderer.

When it dies, it lashes out with a huge explosion in its death throes. Don't let your guard down until the very end.
ze.quest.273.title: Unity
ze.quest.273.subtitle: Mechanical Fusion Anvil
ze.quest.273.des: This is the mechanical anvil used to fuse Cataclysm gear. Its key ingredient is the Witherite obtained from the Harbinger.
ze.quest.274.title: Summon the Calamity
ze.quest.274.subtitle: Wither
ze.quest.274.des:
The Wither does not spawn naturally; it is a powerful monster that must be summoned artificially.

Stack four blocks of Soul Sand in a T shape, then place three Wither Skeleton Skulls on top to summon the Wither.

The Wither flies through the air and hurls Wither Skulls at every living thing around it except the undead, dealing wide-area damage. If any creature is hit by these projectiles, the Wither regains health. Once it drops below half health, the Wither becomes immune to ranged attacks other than guns.

By the way, summoning the Wither is restricted inside colonies.
ze.quest.275.title: Tomb Raider's Paradise
ze.quest.275.subtitle: Cursed Pyramid
ze.quest.275.des:
Guided by the Eye of the Desert, or found rarely in deserts, this giant pyramid is guarded by the Koboleton, dinosaur-shaped enemies made of nothing but bones. To protect itself from tomb raiders, the pyramid is packed with all sorts of traps and powerful enemies.

To awaken the mighty being here, you must brush the suspicious sand (the texture is slightly different) at the center of the pyramid with a Brush.

The enemies here are skeletons, i.e. undead, so weapons enchanted with Smite are recommended. But be careful. Their main combat strategy is knocking the weapon right out of your hand. To counter this, I recommend crafting Sticky Gloves out of slime and wearing them.
ze.quest.276.title: The Pyramid's Two Guardians
ze.quest.276.subtitle: Wadjet and Kobolediator
ze.quest.276.des:
These two skeletons will stand in your way to protect the important one inside from tomb raiders.

The Wadjet is a serpent-shaped skeleton that swings and stabs with an ancient spear and casts magic such as sandstorms.

The Kobolediator is a heavily built skeleton that swings a greatsword made of ancient metal.

Several of each exist inside the pyramid, and a pair of them guards a certain being on the lowest level.
ze.quest.277.title: Night at the Pyramid
ze.quest.277.subtitle: Ancient Remnant
ze.quest.277.des:
As you brush the suspicious sand (the texture is slightly different) inside the pyramid, you can excavate a Desert Necklace. Put this necklace on the Ancient Remnant, guarded by the Wadjet and Kobolediator in the room beneath the huge tower at the center of the pyramid, and the Ancient Remnant will awaken.

Since the Ancient Remnant is nothing but bones, arrows do no damage to it, but Smite enchantments and the like are effective. Still, being a giant dinosaur, every huge movement it makes comes at you as a deadly attack. When it stomps its feet, it creates shockwaves, which you can dodge by jumping. After a loud roar, it generates sandstorms, and touching one of these storms inflicts a debuff called the Curse of the Desert. The Curse of the Desert reverses your movement.

There is a rage gauge beneath its health bar. It charges whenever the Ancient Remnant fails to land a direct attack, and when it is full, the Ancient Remnant goes into a rage charge, rushing forward and dealing massive damage to blocks and creatures alike.
ze.quest.278.title: Archaeology Mod (Not)
ze.quest.278.subtitle: Modern Remnant
ze.quest.278.des:
Defeating the Ancient Remnant gives you a Remnant Skull. Place this skull on the ground to summon the Modern Remnant, and this little dinosaur can be tamed with a Sniffer Egg.

It has high speed, health, and attack power, making it useful for ground combat, and it can be healed with Bones or Koboleton Bones. You can also right-click it to make it follow you, move freely, or stay put. It can even be carried around in a bucket.

When the Modern Remnant dies, it is guaranteed to drop a Remnant Skull. But when you summon it again, you have to tame it again.
ze.quest.279.title: Definitely Not Atlantis
ze.quest.279.subtitle: Sunken City
ze.quest.279.des:
Guided by the Eye of the Abyss, or found rarely in all ocean biomes, this sunken city takes the form of a temple and is guarded by many Deeplings.

You'll be moving around and fighting underwater most of the time, so it's best to prepare for that.
ze.quest.280.title: Call of the Leviathan
ze.quest.280.subtitle: Deepling Priest
ze.quest.280.des:
A Deepling of the priestly class, it swings a ritual dagger or fires a flash from the bladder-like organ on its head, inflicting blindness and damage on its target.

The Ritual Dagger it carries can be used as an ingredient to awaken the creature sleeping in the Sunken City.
ze.quest.281.title: Is This Dark Magic?
ze.quest.281.subtitle: Deepling Warlock
ze.quest.281.des:
A Deepling of the warlock class, it uses magic that makes scorching beams erupt from the floor, and threatens you with a ritual dagger if you get close.

The Ritual Dagger it carries can be used as an ingredient to awaken the creature sleeping in the Sunken City.
ze.quest.282.title: Coral Clump
ze.quest.282.subtitle: Coralssus
ze.quest.282.des:
This monster with a huge body made of coral helps the Deeplings repel intruders in this city.

All of its attacks disable shields, so be careful.

The Coral Chunk obtained from defeating it can be used as an ingredient to awaken the creature sleeping in the Sunken City.
ze.quest.283.title: Being of the Abyss
ze.quest.283.subtitle: Leviathan
ze.quest.283.des:
Offer the Abyss Sacrifice, made from ocean resources including a Ritual Dagger and Coral Chunk, to the Abyssal Altar at the center of the city and the Leviathan will be summoned.

As an aquatic creature, it swims quickly through the water and will grab you in its huge body and attack. The Leviathan is also invincible outside of water, so you must fight it underwater no matter what. However, since it has the nature of a beast, it will also attack ordinary aquatic creatures nearby, so you can sometimes distract it.

Most of its attacks are magic attacks, meaning they ignore armor, so please be careful. One of its main moves, the Abyssal Blast, gathers energy around its tentacles and fires a powerful beam from its mouth. It deals continuous damage to its target and destroys every block that blocks the beam. Sometimes you get seized by its tentacles while it fires the beam directly at you, so watch out.

Additionally, most of the Leviathan's attacks inflict debuffs, but if you've eaten Blessed Amethyst Crab Meat, you become immune to them.
ze.quest.284.title: What on Earth
ze.quest.284.subtitle: Amethyst Crab
ze.quest.284.des:
Rarely found in the Lush Caves biome, this giant crab has a stone shell studded with moss and amethyst. It is generally not aggressive and only fights back when attacked.

It has high health and attack power, and the many vines and water of the Lush Caves where it lives can make the fight tricky.

With the items you get from defeating an Amethyst Crab, you can craft armor, or offer them at an altar to make food that lets you ignore the debuffs of a monster you'll fight later.
ze.quest.285.title: Krabby Patty Recipe (Allegedly)
ze.quest.285.subtitle: Amethyst Altar and Blessed Amethyst Crab Meat
ze.quest.285.des:
Offer the crab meat from an Amethyst Crab at the Amethyst Altar in the Sunken City to obtain Blessed Amethyst Crab Meat.

Eating this meat makes you immune to the debuffs the Leviathan inflicts for a period of time.
ze.quest.286.title: Not Your Average Baby
ze.quest.286.subtitle: Baby Leviathan
ze.quest.286.des:
Place the Abyss Egg obtained from defeating the Leviathan and wait, and a Baby Leviathan will hatch. You can tame this Baby Leviathan by feeding it tropical fish.

It isn't invincible like its mother, but it can move around on land, and even as a baby it bites enemies and shoots beams. Right-click to make it follow you, roam freely, or stay put, and you can carry it around in a water bucket.
ze.quest.287.title: Temple Above the Sea
ze.quest.287.subtitle: Acropolis
ze.quest.287.des:
Guided by the Eye of the Storm, or found rarely above warm oceans, this huge floating temple is home to several powerful seafood-shaped enemies.

You can fight your way up fair and square, or use cheesy tricks like a jetpack to reach the top floor right away and face the mighty being there.
ze.quest.288.title: Deep Freeze
ze.quest.288.subtitle: Frosted Prison
ze.quest.288.des:
Guided by the Eye of the Cursed, or found rarely on snowy plains, this huge fortress is guarded by Draugr, undead monsters.

Most of them take extra damage from Smite enchantments, and dead Draugr are not summoned again. However, tempered by the bitter cold, they are immune to freezing, and each one is a powerful foe.
ze.quest.289.title: Empress of the Storm
ze.quest.289.subtitle: Scylla
ze.quest.289.des:
Right-click the giant anchor on the top floor of the Acropolis to summon Scylla. Armored head to toe, she fights with the giant anchor Ceraunus as her main weapon, calling down lightning and waves.

If you are hit by her wave attack, you get the Wet debuff, and taking a shock attack in that state deals damage that ignores armor.
ze.quest.290.title: Warden
ze.quest.290.subtitle: Aptrgangr
ze.quest.290.des:
This giant Draugr has as much health and armor as its huge body suggests, and attacks by swinging a large axe.

Its follow-up attacks are slow, so I recommend dodging an attack and then fighting back with a weapon enchanted with Smite for extra damage.

Defeating it grants you the key to the sealed room deep inside the prison.
ze.quest.291.title: Berserker
ze.quest.291.subtitle: Maledictus
ze.quest.291.des:
Right-click the center of the sealed door with the strange key obtained from defeating Aptrgangr, and the seal will break, letting you enter the room. At the end of the room is a cursed tombstone, and right-clicking it awakens Maledictus, the most powerful being of this prison and of the Overworld.

He attacks his target rapidly with a fast attack speed, and every time his target is hit, his rage gauge fills and his attack power rises with each increase. When the rage gauge is full, he uses his Annihilation technique. This attack deals damage that ignores armor and can't be blocked even with a shield, so get far away.

He swaps weapons to suit the situation. Normally he uses the twin maces called Annihilators, a cursed bow at range, and he launches wide-area attacks with the giant halberd, the Soul Crusher. The lower his health gets, the more skills he uses.

Fortunately, he is affected by Smite enchantments, has no ability to heal during battle, and inflicts no debuffs on his target. Even so, he is strong.
ze.quest.292.title: Dowsing Machine
ze.quest.292.subtitle: Meteorite Detector
ze.quest.292.des:
Used to find meteorites. Hold it in your hand and the needle points toward a nearby meteorite, and when you reach it, the needle spins round and round.

Some meteorites are buried deep underground.
ze.quest.293.title: Look at This
ze.quest.293.subtitle: Ping
ze.quest.293.des:
With the Ping Wheel mod, press T to place a ping on whatever you're looking at. Other players can see that ping too. To adjust ping settings, press * on the numpad to open the ping menu.

If you set a ping channel, only people on the same channel can see your pings.

By the way, chat is Enter.
ze.quest.294.title: This Totally Counts as No Cheats lol
ze.quest.294.subtitle: Teleport Commands
ze.quest.294.des:
The FTB Essentials mod lets you teleport using commands.

/back teleports you to your location before death or before your last teleport.

/sethome saves the spot you're standing on, and /home teleports you to the saved spot.

/rtp moves you to random coordinates. Don't worry, the Y coordinate is set to the surface, so you won't get stuck anywhere.

/tpa (username) teleports you to that user's location. When you use the command, that player can choose to accept or deny.

All teleport commands have their own cooldowns.
ze.quest.295.title: Land Grab
ze.quest.295.subtitle: Claim Protection
ze.quest.295.des:
The FTB Chunks mod lets you protect territory chunk by chunk. Press M to open the full map, then click the 'Claim Chunks (C)' button at the top left to enter claim mode.

In this mode, click a chunk to claim it, and shift-click to force-load it. Chunk loading can put a strain on the server, so be careful.

Other players can't place or break blocks in claimed chunks, and force-loaded chunks stay loaded whenever the server is running.

To unclaim or unload a chunk, just right-click it.
ze.quest.296.title: We're Bestiez uwu
ze.quest.296.subtitle: Party System
ze.quest.296.des:
The FTB Teams mod lets you form a party. Open your inventory and click the team icon (person shape) at the top left to open the team menu.

Here you can create a party and invite your friends. Players in the same party share quest progress, and can share claimed chunks too.

To invite a friend, click the 'Invite' button in the team menu and enter your friend's username.
ze.quest.297.title: Door to the Void
ze.quest.297.subtitle: End Portal
ze.quest.297.des:
Reading the books you found at the stronghold and solving the mysterious contraptions, you finally reach the place with the portal. You probably beat the Steel Knight, or ran away from him, or something.

Seeing that the portal frame has spaces where something can be slotted in, you deduce that you must insert all the eyes you've collected. But you notice you can't insert two of the same eye, and realize you'll have to find several different kinds of eyes.

Can you really accomplish what the humanity of the past could not?
ze.quest.298.title: Door of Ten Thousand Paths
ze.quest.298.subtitle: Quantum Network Card
ze.quest.298.des:
Unlimited-range Wireless Access Points or Dimensional Access Points demand a lot of Nether Stars, which can be a heavy burden. If you can already build a Quantum Network, this Quantum Network Card will stand in for them.

Insert a Quantum Network Card into a Wireless Terminal, and insert a Quantum Entangled Singularity matching the one in the Quantum Network connected to your AE system, and you can access your AE system from anywhere. The Quantum Network also carries power, so it supplies enough to keep your Wireless Terminal from running out of charge.
ze.quest.299.title: Marker
ze.quest.299.subtitle: Beacon and Radio Kit
ze.quest.299.des:
With a Beacon you can let the outside alien world know where you are. And with a Radio Kit you should be able to communicate with them.

It is expected to take a long time for them to receive your signal and reply. Probably.. about one season..

Also, be careful. Because of the Radio Kit's special frequency, powerful monsters nearby may come swarming.
ze.quest.300.title: Modular Power Suit
ze.quest.300.subtitle: MekaSuit
ze.quest.300.des:
You can craft an electronic cutting-edge suit. Charge it with power and put it on, and when you take damage, the suit absorbs the damage meant for you and consumes power. The MekaTool serves as a pickaxe, axe, and shovel, and has decent attack power.

To use them properly, you need to install each module through the Modification Station.
ze.quest.300.des2: Originally, wearing the chestplate also turns your arm model in first person into the MekaSuit's, but it was modified to show the vanilla arms for compatibility with TacZ mod guns.
ze.quest.301.title: Power Armor Tinker Table
ze.quest.301.subtitle: Modification Station
ze.quest.301.des:
You can apply the modules you want to each MekaSuit piece or tool at the Modification Station.

To see the types of modules, press U on a Module Base to check what it's used for.

To adjust an installed module's performance or settings, press \(|) to open the module settings screen.
ze.quest.302.title: Drinking Hat
ze.quest.302.subtitle: Straw
ze.quest.302.des:
Stick it on a Blaze Burner and it lets the burner suck up liquid directly.

You can connect fluid pipes straight to it. You can pour in a liquid like lava to heat it up, and with oil such as diesel you can even heat it to a superheated state.
ze.quest.303.title: Compact Design
ze.quest.303.subtitle: Fan Catalyst
ze.quest.303.des:
Putting a liquid in front of a fan and designing it so that the liquid doesn't flow elsewhere is quite a hassle. That's why this Fan Catalyst exists.

Place this Fan Catalyst in front of a fan and fill it with the liquid you want. To use fire, place Netherrack and light it on fire.
ze.quest.304.title: Extreme Sports
ze.quest.304.subtitle: Folding Glider
ze.quest.304.des: The Folding Glider works like an Elytra. However, since it uses lightweight materials, its durability wears down quickly. Luckily, you can easily repair it at an anvil with Strong Cloth, which is easy to come by.
ze.quest.305.title: Nutritious Snacks for Our Crops
ze.quest.305.subtitle: Rich Soil
ze.quest.305.des:
Tilling regular dirt and planting seeds is a fine method, but planting seeds in better soil is even better.

Mix dirt with various natural byproducts (monsters are part of nature too) to make organic compost, place it somewhere with plenty of sunlight and moisture, and give it time, and it will slowly turn into Rich Soil.

Crops planted in Rich Soil randomly receive a growth boost at regular intervals and grow much faster.
ze.quest.306.title: Riff-Raff
ze.quest.306.subtitle: Weeds
ze.quest.306.des:
This plant, found in the wild or on the farm you've so lovingly built, is a weed.

It has no real use, and worse, it has the nasty habit of turning nearby crops into weeds, so if you spot one around your farm, get rid of it quickly.
ze.quest.307.title: Where Seeds Grow
ze.quest.307.subtitle: Hoe
ze.quest.307.des:
Most foods require several kinds of vegetables or fruits. To grow them, you have to farm.

Most crops are planted in farmland, and you make farmland by tilling dirt with a hoe.

While crops are growing, there must be water nearby, and they need sunlight or some other light.
ze.quest.308.title: Inventory Management
ze.quest.308.subtitle: ME Requester
ze.quest.308.des:
The ME Requester places auto-crafting requests so that registered items are always kept at the quantity you set. For example, if the stock of Oak Planks falls below the set amount, it sends a crafting request using the registered Oak Planks pattern to craft up to the set quantity.

Connect the ME Requester to your ME system, register the item, fluid, or gas you want in an empty slot of the ME Requester, set the minimum stock under stock quantity so it places a request whenever stock is below that number, and set the craft quantity to decide how much to make each time it places a request. When you're done, click the check icon on the right to apply the changes.

You can manage the list of all the requests you've applied through the ME Requester Terminal.
ze.quest.309.title: Building Tools
ze.quest.309.subtitle: Building, Exchanging, and Copy-Paste Gadgets
ze.quest.309.des:
These tools make building much easier. Generally, they work as long as they're charged with power and you have materials.

The Building Gadget lets you set a block shape based on the direction you're facing and place it with a right-click.

The Exchanging Gadget lets you swap a range of blocks you're looking at for another block.

The Copy-Paste Gadget lets you right-click and sneak right-click to select a range, then copy the blocks in that range and paste them somewhere else.

To learn how to use each tool, hold it and long-press G to open the UI.
ze.quest.310.title: Time Is Money (Bill Gates Edition)
ze.quest.310.subtitle: Waiting
ze.quest.310.des:
In roughly 6 days (2 hours), the alien faction nearby is expected to contact you.

Their language may differ a bit from yours, but the PDA you're looking at now has an auto-translate function, so communication shouldn't be a big problem.

Have you thought about what to do if they turn out to be hostile? ... For now, preparing some bullets and syringes might not be a bad idea.
ze.quest.311.title: Debut
ze.quest.311.subtitle: Communication
ze.quest.311.des:
(Translated by PDA) We have detected the signal you sent up. We are members of the Galactic Union.

Our expedition team is heading to the Overworld where you are located, but it will take quite a lot of time. Before that, we propose trade with you through a small-scale long-range transfer system. According to our data, your world has rare creatures and valuable resources.

This radio channel is not very secure, so we will contact you directly through your PDA. You no longer need to use the radio. If you wish for peaceful communication with us, please accept on your PDA.
ze.quest.312.title: Hulk
ze.quest.312.subtitle: Mutant Zombie
ze.quest.312.des:
(Translated by PDA) We are collecting specimens of mutant monsters. Defeat them and send us the data. We will provide rewards accordingly.

According to the information we have, the Mutant Zombie's cells divide rapidly before it dies and it revives. To prevent this, you must set it on fire as it falls.
ze.quest.313.title: Hunter
ze.quest.313.subtitle: Mutant Skeleton
ze.quest.313.des:
(Translated by PDA) We are collecting specimens of mutant monsters. Defeat them and send us the data. We will provide rewards accordingly.

According to the information we have, when the Mutant Skeleton dies, its fragments scatter in all directions. If you gather those fragments, you can craft some quite useful armor.
ze.quest.314.title: Look at the Size of That Thing! It Must Be Loaded With Gunpowder!
ze.quest.314.subtitle: Mutant Creeper
ze.quest.314.des:
(Translated by PDA) We are collecting specimens of mutant monsters. Defeat them and send us the data. We will provide rewards accordingly.

According to the information we have, when the Mutant Creeper dies, it pulls in nearby creatures, causes a massive explosion, and then leaves behind a single egg. If you take good care of that egg, a small Creeper will hatch.
ze.quest.315.title: Slender Man
ze.quest.315.subtitle: Mutant Enderman
ze.quest.315.des:
(Translated by PDA) We are collecting specimens of mutant monsters. Defeat them and send us the data. We will provide rewards accordingly.

According to the information we have, when the Mutant Enderman dies, it pulls in nearby creatures and self-destructs, unleashing all the power it had stored.
ze.quest.317.title: Archaeology Mod, Minus the Dinosaurs
ze.quest.317.subtitle: Fossil Excavation
ze.quest.317.des:
(Translated by PDA) The Overworld is full of creatures not found even on other planets. Their fossils hold great research value for us.

Carefully excavate fossil-bearing dirt with a Brush and bones will emerge. Most will be broken from the ravages of time, but some bones will remain nearly intact.
ze.quest.318.title: Buried Guardian
ze.quest.318.subtitle: Guardian Fossil
ze.quest.318.des:
(Translated by PDA) According to our information, the Guardian is a unique creature that defends its structures underwater and attacks intruders with magical power.

If a Guardian Fossil is nearby, you can gain a Water Breathing effect. Perhaps the Guardians of that era were friendly to humans.
ze.quest.319.title: The Real Dinosaur
ze.quest.319.subtitle: Chicken Fossil
ze.quest.319.des:
(Translated by PDA) According to our information, the chickens in the Overworld today are probably genetically modified. But it is presumed that unmodified chickens lived there in the past.

If you are near a Chicken Fossil, you can gain a Slow Falling effect. It seems chickens couldn't fly back then either.
ze.quest.320.title: Wolf MC
ze.quest.320.subtitle: Wolf Fossil
ze.quest.320.des:
(Translated by PDA) According to our information, the wolves in the Overworld today are relatively tame by nature and easy to domesticate. But it is presumed that there were more wolves with strong wild instincts there in the past.

A Wolf Fossil drives away nearby Skeletons. Presumably, the wolves of that era also hunted Skeletons.
ze.quest.321.title: Ancient Villager
ze.quest.321.subtitle: Villager Fossil
ze.quest.321.des:
(Translated by PDA) According to our information, the intelligent life form representing the Overworld today is judged to be a bipedal mammal called a Villager. In the past, they appear to have had a more hunched posture.

You can make a Villager Fossil hold something. It is presumed that Villagers of that era could also grab and use things.
ze.quest.322.title: Cats Back in the Day
ze.quest.322.subtitle: Ocelot Fossil
ze.quest.322.des:
(Translated by PDA) The Ocelot is a feline, an agile and wary animal. According to our information, in the past Ocelots in the Overworld could be tamed like cats. Perhaps that technique has been lost, as taming is now impossible, but cats have taken their place instead. Perhaps tamed Ocelots are today's cats.

An Ocelot Fossil drives away nearby Creepers. This fact could be evidence that Ocelots and cats are closely related. ... Or you could say an Ocelot is simply nothing more than a feline.
ze.quest.323.title: To Some, It Could Be a Handle..
ze.quest.323.subtitle: Sheep Fossil
ze.quest.323.des:
(Translated by PDA) According to our information, the sheep in the Overworld today are domesticated sheep. That's why they have no horns. The sheep of the Overworld's past are presumed to have had horns.

Right-click a Sheep Fossil to hear the unique sounds the horns make. Maybe goats descended from the sheep of the past?
ze.quest.324.title: Uncontrollable Explosion
ze.quest.324.subtitle: Creeper Fossil
ze.quest.324.des:
(Translated by PDA) The Creeper, an unknown monster that exists only in the Overworld, is presumed to have been appearing in the Overworld since long ago.

If you place a Creeper Fossil.. ominous particles just appear around it. Also, there was TNT inside its body, apparently.
ze.quest.326.title: Steeping Time
ze.quest.326.subtitle: Kettle
ze.quest.326.des:
You can boil certain plants in water to steep tea. You'll need to supply heat from below, such as a stove, and add the liquid and items that match the recipe.

You can automate it by attaching pipes and the like. Items can be fed in from the top, and liquids can be piped in and out from the sides. It's ugly, but.. being automatable is the good part, right?
ze.quest.327.title: Squeezing Blood From a Stone
ze.quest.327.subtitle: Quest Screen
ze.quest.327.des:
(Translated by PDA) We're glad to see you're being friendly. From now on, the teams in each division of our faction will be contacting you. Before that, a few preparations will be needed for smoother exchange of information and resources.

Right now, our small-scale teleport technology lets us exchange goods with you, but things without a fixed form, like liquids or electric power, can't be delivered. Repeatedly sending and receiving large quantities is also out of the question. To solve this, we recommend crafting a Quest Screen.

Place the Quest Screen, designate what you'll be sending us, then connect pipes or cables to it.

If you don't have any equipment that can produce liquid pipes or power.. you'd better get some ready.
ze.quest.328.title: The Flow of Electrons
ze.quest.328.subtitle: Submit Electricity
ze.quest.328.des:
